lead: The Follower makes the pursuit the whole shape of you. The Mane opens the spread wide enough for anyone to help themselves. you are visibly behind and visibly at ease, and nobody has ever put those two together.
sun: the pursuit is the thing you are, and it will only certify what came hard. everything that lands easy gets set aside unweighed, and with the spread open, a great deal lands easy. so the record you keep of yourself has almost nothing in it, and it stays thin on purpose: closing the gap would end the pursuit and leave you standing on a pile of things that were simply handed over.
moon: day to day you are open, and open things get used. people draw on you without asking, which is what a spread invites, and you let it run, because objecting would mean stepping up to a position you spent years declining. the ease is real, and it is also why nothing you do reads as effort: what looks this comfortable never gets counted as work, by them or by you.
pull: you have been given a great deal and you are still, by your own accounting, empty-handed. the pursuit does not accept deliveries. only what you had to go and take.
tension: nobody who calls you easygoing is wrong about the surface, and nobody has been under it. a good week for the half of you that receives is a lost week for the half that is chasing, and both halves are having it at the same time. you can keep an account open on someone for years while staying warm to them throughout, so they never learn there is an account, and it never gets closed.
cost: you are unusually good at being drawn on, steadily, by a lot of people, not one of whom would believe it took anything out of you. underneath, a tally runs item by item, kept by someone everybody describes as having nothing to complain about. it stays where it is. producing it would cost you the description, and the description is the whole arrangement.

lead: you are already helping before the sentence asking for it is finished, and every one of those first seconds is permanent. you move fastest exactly where you can take back least.
sun: no undo attaches itself to your first response, which is the one made with the least information anyone will ever have. everyone else revises as the thing resolves; you had already committed at your loudest before the shape of it was clear, and the correction you would make an hour later has nowhere to land. the first version is the one that stayed in the room.
moon: the opening does not wait for confirmation before it commits, and it has never needed to, because an opening costs nothing to repeat. this sun charges for every one. so the false starts accumulate as permanent marks on people who were never in trouble, and you cannot go back afterward and unsay a rescue that nobody required.
pull: you arrive before the facts do and you arrive at full size, so the people you reach fastest are the ones who get the least considered version of you, permanently.
tension: reckless comes from people who have watched exactly one of these go wrong. what follows is quieter: they stop telling you early. news reaches you assembled, after the decisions are made, because handing you a half-formed problem sets off a full-sized response nobody can retract. so you are last to know in the one situation you were built to be first in, and nobody tells you that is why.
cost: in a real emergency you are already moving while everyone else is still deciding whether it counts, and you commit the whole of yourself without waiting to be asked. the bill comes due on the ordinary days. every door you shoved open stays open, and you are not the one who lives in the room behind it, and the people who do live there date the draft to you.

lead: there is a place inside you nobody has ever audited. what The Storm eventually lets out of it comes once, whole, at a size set by the length of The Bearer's holding rather than by whatever finally tipped it.
sun: no undo removes the small version from your options. a sentence let out early to test the water is still a sentence that cannot be recalled, so every trial run lands as permanently as the real thing, and you never learn how another person would take what you are holding. silence is the only reversible move available to you, and it stays reversible for years, which is exactly how it wins.
moon: what is carried, held against this sun, stops being patience and becomes containment. you are the only person who knows the current size of it, and from outside the holding reads as an even temper. people build on that. they make arrangements that assume the calm is the whole of you, and you let them, because correcting it would mean showing them the contents.
pull: you are the easiest person anyone knows to live with, right up until the one afternoon that settles what you were, and nothing after it gets weighed against the twenty years.
tension: from where they stand, out of proportion is accurate — they were handed the last item, not the pile it landed on. the pile cannot be produced afterward as evidence, because a list of things nobody heard at the time lands as a second charge rather than a defence. so one afternoon becomes your temper, and the years of holding underneath it are counted as nothing at all.
cost: you can be handed the thing that must not move, and nobody checks on it again — not in year one, not in year six, not on the night someone offers you a reason to set it down. nothing you contain gets answered; none of it arrives small enough to answer. the only part of you that reaches anyone arrives whole and closes the conversation on its way in.

lead: The Gathered Stars are several and get counted as one, and The Storm signs for all of them — whichever part of you moves, the mark goes under a single name and the rest are bound by it.
sun: no undo means the part of you that moved did not need agreement from the others, and cannot be overruled by them afterward. the act is already outside, where the count is one. so your interior arguments have no jurisdiction over your record — whichever of you acted has set the position for all of you, and the ones who dissented keep dissenting inside a life that has already gone the other way.
moon: the many as one collapses under a mark that will not come off. people who would eventually have resolved you into the several you actually are stop at the version that did the damage, and stay there. so the plural stays interior. you go on running the full committee in private while every room you enter is dealing with a single, well-documented person who is one of them.
pull: one of you did it and all of you are serving it, and the room outside has never once been told there is more than one of you.
tension: two different people is what gets said, and it gets said by both halves of the room. the ones who know the quiet version hear about the mark and decide they were being managed. the ones who only have the mark treat every calm month afterward as the performance. neither group is wrong about what they saw, and there is no account you can give that covers both without one of them sounding invented.
cost: you can commit without being unanimous, which is why you move while everyone else is still waiting for all of themselves to agree. the price is the record. every permanent thing with your name on it was decided by whichever of you was loudest that hour, and the ones who would have done it otherwise have no way to be known, because nothing they wanted ever left a mark.

lead: The Storm makes everything you do final. The Follower keeps you one length back on purpose. so the biggest, least reversible things in your life all happen from a position you have decided never to leave.
sun: the full-force version keeps landing on bystanders who were never the target. what leaves you is sized against someone standing outside the room entirely, and it goes into whoever is present at exactly that size, complete, unrecallable. they take the full weight of a comparison they were never told about, and afterward you cannot walk it back without naming the person you were measuring against.
moon: underneath, the position behind was taken at the same volume as everything else, so it does not retract either. you cannot quietly stop keeping the distance. and the account runs at full size, item by item, nothing on it ageing down: a slight from a decade back is still at the loudness it arrived with, and nobody else in the room can hear it.
pull: nothing you do arrives small, and nothing you do closes the distance, because the one you measure against has never been close enough to see any of it land.
tension: loyal gets said about you, and intense, and nobody has connected the two. what you give arrives at a size nobody asked for and cannot be handed back without a scene, so it is accepted warmly and the debt settles on the wrong side of the room. the same force runs the other direction at the same size — a withdrawal here has never once been reversed, and everyone learns that early.
cost: holding a position for years with nothing coming back is something you do without visible strain — you can stay behind someone through a decade that gave you no reason to. nothing you have ever kept has been allowed to fade. the injuries are filed at their original volume, permanently, and the filing is not a choice you get to revisit.

lead: The Blaze finds the thing, The Storm enters it at full force, and then the search moves on. what you leave behind you is permanent, and you are almost never present for the part where that becomes obvious.
sun: curiosity at this size is never light. you go into a subject, a person, a city, at the depth of someone settling there, and everything you touch is altered to that depth. from the other side the intensity reads as commitment and nothing else — nobody has ever been entered that far by somebody who was only passing through, so they file it as the beginning of something.
moon: the search does not slow down for what the entering cost anybody. the moment the thing is known you are finished with it, and finished arrives fast, faster than the wreckage becomes visible. so you are always leaving a place still rearranging itself around you, in good conscience, because from inside there was no decision to leave — there was just the next thing, and it was already interesting.
pull: leaving was never the decision. the search simply ended, and the room you were standing in is still shaped like the night you came in.
tension: you get called a tourist, and worse, by people who were there for the part where you were more present than anyone they had met. both descriptions are of you, three weeks apart, and neither one is wrong. explaining the sequence requires admitting that the intensity was real and temporary at once, which sounds like a defence, so you take the word and let it stand, and the next place gets the same full arrival.
cost: the first pass at anything gets you further than most people manage in a year — you arrive at full force, and full force opens doors that politeness never will. you never get a second year of anything. the depth you go to on the way in makes every exit a demolition, so the places that would have taken you back are gone, behind you.

lead: nothing here answers The Storm. no second setting, no part of you that goes in halfway — what you do in public and what you are alone are the same size, and both of them are final.
sun: a room gets one reading of you and it is complete on first contact. there is no gentler version arriving later to soften the first one, no evidence that the size was situational, so people calibrate to the largest thing they have seen you do and stay calibrated there. what you meant as one hard week becomes the standing description, and every later kindness gets read as an exception to it.
moon: inside, nothing gets a draft. the first version of a feeling is the only version, and it arrives at full size with no committee behind it — no cooler part watching from the side, no delay in which the thing could be sized down before it becomes what you are doing. you find out what you decided at the same moment everybody else does.
pull: no second opinion about yourself has ever arrived in time. the first thing you feel is the thing you do, and by the time you know it, it is already someone else's history.
tension: all or nothing gets said about you as though it named a choice you keep making. people have only ever met you at one size because there is no other size to meet, and you cannot show range by having some — the only demonstration available is restraint, which reads as sulking. so everyone around you decides early, from one incident, how much of you they can take, and they never mention having decided.
cost: nobody has to wonder where you stand, ever, on anything — you are the person a crisis can be handed to whole, because there is no part of you that will hedge it. you have no small correction available. every adjustment you make is a reversal at full size, so you accumulate a history of enormous turns, and no record at all of having changed your mind gently.

lead: The Storm leaves a mark that does not lift, and The Return walks back in a year later expecting the room to have kept a place. both are you, and only one of them is on anyone's record.
sun: no undo covers the coming back as well. you cannot send a return ahead in miniature — no message that opens the door a crack and gets withdrawn if the answer comes cold. the re-entry lands at the same size the leaving did, and it commits the other person again, whole, before either of you has worked out whether the second time was wanted.
moon: what comes back sits underneath as an assumption rather than a hope, so a rupture never quite files as an ending — it files as an interval. you do not do the mourning at the time. then you arrive back into rooms that finished mourning you a year ago, carrying no version of events in which the thing was over.
pull: nothing you have done has ever felt final from the inside, and all of it was final from theirs. you hold the only copy of the version where everyone comes back.
tension: you think you can just walk back in gets said, and it is a fair account of what you did. what cannot be entered as a defence is that you were never pretending the thing had not happened — you had no ending on file for it. so people close things with you formally now, out loud, with a date, because they have learned that anything gentler reads to you as a pause.
cost: you can walk back into a room where the worst thing happened and start it again, which most people cannot do at all — the apology arrives whole and means exactly what it says. each of those returns is another permanent thing done to somebody. the ones who keep taking you back are collecting them, and not one can be handed back.

lead: The Ghost puts no edge on what goes out of you, so the size stays invisible on both sides, yours included. what anyone can point to is the day it stopped, and that day does not come off.
sun: no undo removes the taper. what leaves you leaves at full size — never a season of becoming slightly less available, never a quiet reduction down to something you could keep doing. the only smaller amount on offer is nothing at all, and arriving at nothing is an event, whole, on someone who has been living off the larger number for years.
moon: the haze that feeds shows no level. neither of you can see how much is going out — not the person taking it, who was never shown an edge, and not you, who finds out the amount only when it runs out. a warning would need a number, and neither of you has ever held one, so the stop reaches you both as news.
pull: you have one setting for giving and one for stopping, and the people who ate for years remember only the second, because it is the only one that left anything behind.
tension: you cut people off is the sentence, and it comes with names attached, and the names are right. what does not appear beside them is the decade underneath each one, because feeding leaves no mark on anything — soft work never does. so the account everyone can consult holds one entry per person, the last one, and the rest sits with you alone, where it reads as self-defence the moment you produce it.
cost: you can carry someone through years of something and never once mention that you are carrying them, at a size they will never be able to estimate. the ones you carried longest are the ones the ending lands on hardest — a decade of it comes off in one evening, and neither of you can make that evening smaller or undo it afterwards.

lead: The Glance reads the ending off a pause nobody else registered, and The Storm closes the thing on the spot at full size, months before anyone would have called it. both moves are one motion.
sun: no undo sizes the response to what you can see arriving rather than to what has actually happened, and what has actually happened is a pause, a tone, a name gone quiet on a thread. so what leaves you is out of proportion to the visible event every time, permanently, and it stays on the record in that shape, while the thing you were answering never becomes anything anyone else can point at.
moon: contact that holds means the noticing never gets said while it is still small. you keep it instead, and keeping it is not neutral on this sun — held things gain size here. by the time it leaves you it has stopped being a question about a pause and become a finding about a person, delivered whole, with months of private corroboration behind it.
pull: you see it going months before anyone says so, and then you make it go, and the only evidence you were right is the damage.
tension: the word that gets used is paranoid, and there is no answer to it. you cannot produce a pause. you cannot produce three weeks of someone being fractionally more careful with you, and if you could, it would sound like the case of a person assembling one. so the people near you learn to manage their tone, which removes the only instrument you had, and nobody mentions doing it.
cost: you are never the last to know, and you do not spend a year inside an arrangement that finished months ago — you are out ahead of the announcement, on your own terms, whole. every ending in your life has your own hand on it, and none of them gets lighter for that. contact that holds does not stop holding because you were the one who cut it.

lead: The Storm puts something into the room that will not come out again, and The Throne keeps your face still while it lands, so it arrives looking chosen in advance, at leisure, by someone comfortable.
sun: no undo lands differently when the room cannot see it costing you anything. scale gets pardoned when it visibly takes something out of the person on the way through, and the seat will not let any of that show. so the size of what you did is entered as the size of what you meant — to the inch, deliberately, by a person who was not overtaken.
moon: then the chair takes it private. what cannot be recalled gets added to the one question you have never put to another person out loud — whether the seat is yours by right or only by occupancy — and the same bearing that keeps you upright in the room is what makes the question unaskable, because asking it would be the flinch.
pull: you are never seen deciding, only seen having decided, so the worst hour of your life stands in the record with your posture on it and no evidence that it took you by surprise.
tension: cold gets said early and then stops being said, because the room has already adjusted: the mess is handled where you will not see it, the honest account of the evening is edited before it reaches you, and nobody hands you the bill for the last one. so the true weight of what you do arrives only as rumour, and the next one leaves at exactly the size the last one did.
cost: you can end a thing and then remain in the same chair while everyone rearranges around the ending — say the sentence, hold the posture, stay in the building. apologies, though, have to look like they cost the person making them, and yours never will, so the ones you owe cannot be paid, and the people owed them wait, and then stop.

lead: The Mane keeps you visible and comfortable being visible, and The Storm hands you a record that cannot be edited, so your least reversible hour happened before an audience that had already gathered.
sun: no undo does not agree to be a rumour here. what you did was done where the whole room could watch it, and the room is one you had spent years making easy to enter — so the people carrying the account are the same ones who came to you for rest. the permanent thing is filed by witnesses who liked you, which is the version that travels furthest.
moon: the spread has no partial setting. after something permanent, most people go a degree quieter and keep a corner of themselves out of the room; you have no corner. so you go on hosting the person you damaged, at the same warmth, because the only alternative available to you is closing the whole of it — and a closed version of you reads to everyone else as a confession.
pull: what came easily is filed as a gift, and the one thing nobody has called a gift is the damage, which makes it the only part of your life you are certain you authored.
tension: the word is spoiled, and it gets used by people who watched things come to you and did not watch you decline any of them. then the permanent thing happens and the word changes: what was ease becomes evidence that you were never checked, that nothing ever told you no, and the scale of what you did gets explained by everything you were handed. neither account leaves room for effort, and you have stopped offering one.
cost: you can hand someone the whole of a room and mean it, at a size other people ration across years, without asking them to earn it first. nothing is kept aside, though. there is no held-out portion of you to rebuild from, so when a permanent thing costs you the room, it costs you the only version of yourself that was ever in use.

lead: The Turning lets you finish a whole version of yourself and walk out of it. The Storm does not let what that version did travel with you: it stays where it happened, still signed, still yours.
sun: no undo does not participate in the turnover. every other part of a finished stretch goes with it — the flat, the work, the people you were at your worst around — and the permanent things stay put, dated and attached, in the possession of whoever was standing there. so the only continuous thing about you is a record made entirely of stretches you are done with.
moon: the weather breaks and takes the whole of the person who did it, leaving every obligation that person incurred sitting in the new life, itemised. so you owe things you cannot feel any connection to owing. from inside it is honest — that was another season entirely. from outside there is someone who did something permanent and then simply stopped being available to hold it.
pull: you shed completely and the mark does not shed, so you keep arriving new in rooms that are still holding the thing you can no longer feel having done.
tension: people wait for remorse and what arrives is payment. you meet the obligation, on time, in full, from a version of yourself with no memory of wanting to do the thing — and paying without feeling it lands as an insult, because what was wanted was the part where you are still in there suffering. so the debt gets settled and the grievance does not, and it stays open for decades on a matter you consider closed.
cost: you can finish something completely — no residue, no version of it running in a spare room — which most people never manage once. the credit stays with the version that earned it. the good years leave when their season does, and nothing you built follows you into the next life. only the permanent things cross, and they are the ones you would have left if leaving were on offer.

lead: other people date the start of their lives to an afternoon you cannot recall. The Hand puts a push out without weighing it; The Storm keeps it at the weight it went out with, forever.
sun: no undo settles on the push rather than on the thing made. a bad chair can be broken up; the motion you started in another person cannot — it went out of you undiminished and runs now on their legs, under their name. the half-serious sentence and the considered one arrive identical, both permanent, and you have never been able to tell which is which on the way out.
moon: the maker's hand keeps no receipt. what has left the palm is not counted here, so you carry no list of what you started, while every person you started is keeping an exact one, dated. gratitude arrives years later for a thing you did not know you did, and so does the invoice, and you take both blind, from people who assume you remember.
pull: you handed it over once, without counting, and it cannot be handed back. the people running on it remember the afternoon exactly. your side of it is blank.
tension: people call you generous, and they mean it kindly, and not one has worked out that the praise describes an absence of counting. the trouble comes when one of the pushes went somewhere bad. you cannot show that it was one of forty, because the other thirty-nine left no record anywhere, so the single wrecked life stands alone as the complete account of what your hand does, and there is nothing to set beside it.
cost: you can put a person into motion in a single conversation, which almost nobody can do, and you do it without needing the credit or the outcome. no version of you meets someone and leaves them as found, so every casual afternoon is capable of permanent work, and you find out which ones were, later, from them.

lead: there is no draft. what you make arrives finished, shown, and out of reach in one motion. The Jewel puts nothing over it on the way out, and nothing seen under The Storm becomes unseen later.
sun: the permanence lands on the showing, not the making. a thing put out to see how it reads cannot be quietly taken down here — the first version is the public one, and it stays the public one after you have learned what was wrong with it. so you are held to work you finished before you were good, by people who saw it once and filed it, whole.
moon: the undefended part is not a choice made fresh each time; guarding simply does not occur to you until the thing is already gone. and what admiration wants here is access, which you grant at full size on the first ask, permanently — so the people closest to the work are the ones who arrived because of it, and you have never met the version of them that came before.
pull: everything good you have made is out there without you standing over it, and the only reason most of it is still yours is that nobody has come for it yet.
tension: the people who watched you hand over the thing, and then hand over the explanation of how it was done, came away calling you naive. it sticks because you cannot demonstrate otherwise without one permanent hard act, and a single hard act from someone with your record reads as a change of character rather than an overdue no. so the description survives, and the taking continues, and both are now facts about you.
cost: you can finish a thing and let it go into the world at its full size without first working out who it protects you from, which is why what you make has an ease in it that guarded work never has. the beautiful thing goes out unmarked and unrecallable, and the account of who made it is settled later by whoever is holding it.

lead: every room that remembers you exactly is a room you were never a member of. the permanent things get done at full size in places that never held a file on you, and afterwards they hold exactly one.
sun: no undo runs the other way here too: the cover only lifts once. whatever gets out about you — the thing you did, the thing you wanted — cannot be put back under, and going quiet afterwards does not restore it, it only removes you from the room where the account is being settled. the leaving itself is loud, and the version left behind is the last one anybody got.
moon: standing apart was never a decision, which leaves no group to close around you now. other people have a set of witnesses who will say it was unlike them; you have a series of rooms, each holding one complete event and nothing before it. nobody near you has enough of the sequence to put the permanent thing in any order but the worst one.
pull: you have never belonged to anything that could hold a piece of your record for you, so every permanent thing you have done is filed by strangers, entire and out of context.
tension: secretive lands oddly on someone who has hidden nothing at all — you simply never handed anyone the running commentary, and years of it cannot be supplied afterwards. once something permanent happens, that gap does the work of a motive. people fill it plausibly, arguing with the filling sounds like confirming it, and what they assembled is the only account on file.
cost: you can do the thing nobody in the room will sign off on, because nobody's sign-off was ever load-bearing for you — no permission was needed going in and none is missed coming out. nothing corroborates you. the single event outweighs every long acquaintance you have, and it is permanent, so the shortest version of you is the durable one.

lead: halfway through ending it you are also renewing it. both moves went in whole, both are on the record, and neither can be walked back. The Claws never pick. The Storm charges for both.
sun: permanence does not discriminate between the two directions; it takes them both, in full, and keeps them. so you cannot let one of the pair quietly lapse — the side you stopped attending to is still signed for, still standing where you left it, still yours. the record holds you doing the thing and undoing it at identical weight, and no later act has ever been able to demote either entry.
moon: from inside, the fork has never once felt like hedging — each side of you goes the whole way in, and means it, and signs. so one party is holding a complete and unrecallable commitment with their name on it, and the party opposite is holding one exactly like it. both are genuine. only one survives being read aloud.
pull: two people are each holding a version of you that went all the way in, both of them accurate, neither of them recallable, and speaking for one of them makes the other a lie.
tension: each side has seen one of your commitments in full and only heard about the other, which is where two-faced comes from. anything you say in explanation of the second arrives as a defence of the first, so the explaining stops early. each side keeps a permanent record of getting everything, and a rumour that somebody else did too, and neither record was ever wrong.
cost: you can hold two opposed things at their full weight for years without either one thinning — the marriage and the exit, the loyalty and the case against it, both funded, neither faked. nobody extends you the benefit of the doubt anymore. every permanent thing you do is evidence for the opposite thing you also did, and it will be used that way, by both sides, forever.

lead: the biggest promise of your life has never come back up for a second decision. The Crown does not offer one, and under The Storm a departure would be the largest and least recallable thing you ever did.
sun: a promise made here has no trial run. there is no small first version to offer, watch for a season and quietly withdraw — no undo takes that off the table, so the terms go in whole, on one afternoon, at the volume of that afternoon. what governs the next forty years was fixed by whoever you happened to be for an hour.
moon: a bond built to outlast the feeling will outlast this too. the day you were at full size lands inside an arrangement with no release clause, so the person on the other end absorbs it and stays, because staying is what they do here. the injury gets housed rather than settled, and the housing was built to hold for decades.
pull: you have never lost anyone, and you have never been forgiven by anyone either — the bond just holds, with the whole record sitting inside it, unpaid.
tension: the people who call it solid have never had to leave one. from inside, the bond does not resolve anything — it stores. every hour that could not be taken back is still in the room, unanswered, with the arrangement running over the top of it. what looks from outside like a thing that survived is a thing that was never given the option of ending, by either of you.
cost: what you hold, holds. through decades, through stretches that gave you nothing back, without any part of you quietly shopping for the exit — and people can feel that, and they build on it. nothing ever clears, though. no one you hurt has had to decide whether to keep you, so no one has chosen you a second time, and the first choice is still doing all the work.

lead: nobody has stood above you since you were young, and nothing you did from up there can be taken back — the room has been running for years on rules you set in one bad hour and never revisited.
sun: no undo comes with no one above it. most people do the permanent thing and then meet someone senior who absorbs it, shrinks it, tells the room it was an aberration; you have been that person since before you were ready, so what leaves you goes onto the record unmediated, and no one's job is to say that was not the standard.
moon: the eldest does not get corrected. deference arrives before your sentence is finished, so the weight of what you do is never reported back to you — the room adjusts around it and says nothing. and it gets copied. what you did at full volume becomes the way things are done here, carried on by people who were not there and cannot say where they learned it.
pull: nobody has ever told you how big you are, and the room below is already doing it your way, at your volume, and calling it normal.
tension: heavy-handed gets said once, early, by someone who then stops saying it, and after that nothing about your size comes back to you in words. it comes back as imitation. the sharpest people under you learn the register and use it on each other, and when it goes badly there it is still your sentence in their mouths, at your volume, dated to a night none of them attended.
cost: you can take the whole weight of a thing the moment it goes wrong, in front of everyone, without checking whether it is yours to take — and it settles the room instantly, because someone senior said it out loud. no true account of yourself comes back from that room. the only mirror available has adopted your worst hour as procedure and will never mention doing it.

lead: halfway down, with the thing in pieces on the floor and the real reason still one layer under that — The Root does not stop where the answer would have been survivable, and The Storm does not put anything back.
sun: no undo attaches to the finding, not just to the digging. once the cause under the cause is said out loud at full size, nobody can go back to not knowing it — the working version everyone was living inside is gone the moment you produce the true one. you get asked why something failed and you answer permanently, and the answer keeps operating in people long after the failure has stopped mattering.
moon: the bottom of it has no stopping rule, and this sun charges for every step past the point where enough was known. so the excavation runs on into things that were holding weight — an arrangement that worked, an account of a childhood, a person's reason for staying — and each one comes apart at the size of everything else you do. nothing comes apart provisionally here.
pull: you find what was actually holding the thing up, every time, and hand it whole to people who were managing perfectly well without it, and the managing stops there.
tension: obsessive is the kindest thing anyone calls it. the invitations change after that: nothing still functioning gets brought near you, because everyone has seen what a look from you costs, and a working arrangement is not something people gamble. so you are called in after collapse, only after, and by then the accuracy is free — nobody needs the cause of a thing that has already finished.
cost: you go all the way down in a single pass and come back with it whole — no staged version, nothing held back while you check how it lands. a mistake goes out at the weight of a finding. every structure you have understood completely is one that no longer stands, including the ones you were living inside, and none of it goes back up.

lead: your moon sits fourteen along from your sun, the far side of the twenty-eight — so The Flock does its arriving and leaving from the exact point your year is measured against, and nothing it does there is small.
sun: the sorting stops being private the moment it leaves you. you have known for years which parts of a household or a crew are load-bearing and which are ornament, and nothing leaves you in a small way, so it goes out whole, once, and the people in it learn their own standing at full volume, and no undo holds the ranking exactly where it landed.
moon: you are staying and going in the same gesture, so nobody around you has ever had a whole person to weigh — and what they do get from you cannot be taken back. your inner life keeps its address at the far point of the year: the full moon nearest your birthday comes up in exactly that place, lighting the half of you the group was never shown.
pull: you belong to them from a distance of half the circle, and the day you say which of them mattered, it is said once and it holds.
tension: you were only ever half here gets said, and it gets said by people who had all of your attention for years. from where they stand, one true sentence about who was carrying the place cancels every good year before it. and you cannot take the sentence back or stay to soften it, so it goes on working in the group after you — the ranking outlives the person who noticed it.
cost: you can walk into a group and see, inside a week, which of them is carrying it and which is being carried — and you can say so, once, at a size that settles the question for good. the year after is the part you never see. the sorting stands, the people go on living under it, and you are already at the far side, arriving somewhere else.

lead: twenty years of open ground and then a single unrecallable hour on it — The Empty District, furnished once by The Storm, and that one item is now the whole description anybody has of you.
sun: no undo lands here with nothing beside it to absorb the weight. other people's permanent things sit among furniture — the work, the opinions, the thing they always say — and get read against all of it. yours arrives into a clearing, where it becomes the only object in view, so one hour reads as the whole visible extent of you rather than as a part of it.
moon: the blank does not learn, either. you clear the same space for the same people the following year, at the same size, because holding it open is the one move available to you that costs nothing to repeat. everything else you do is charged once and kept, so the hosting runs unlimited and the objecting has a single ruinous setting.
pull: you have been available to everybody for twenty years, and available leaves nothing behind. the one afternoon you wanted something for yourself is the only date anybody can give.
tension: space does not appear on anyone's list of what they were given. people remember the year they got through and not the place they got through it in, so two decades of holding open ground registers as having had little else on. then the hour you took some of it back arrives at full size, dated, attached to your name — the one event in a life otherwise made of what you left for other people.
cost: you can take in whatever a person brings without shaping it on the way through — no correction, no version rearranged to suit you. a preference of your own comes out at one size only. it arrives whole, cannot be withdrawn, and lands as a demand however mildly it was meant, so the first one teaches everybody that the space had an owner.

lead: what somebody meant, rather than what they said, is what you answer — and the answer goes out whole and unrecallable, sized to a sentence that was never spoken aloud and can be honestly denied.
sun: no undo takes away the checking question. is this what you meant is the small move that makes hearing safe, and nothing you say comes out small. anything you put in the open commits you to your reading of a person, at volume, for good. so you go from what you heard to what you did about it in one step, and the interpretation is never tested before it becomes an act.
moon: the intake has no lid. you go on receiving what is under the sentence whether or not you can afford to act on it, and every available reply is priced the same, so a backlog builds — years of accurate hearing spent on nothing, because the smallest thing you could have said was already permanent.
pull: you hear everything and can only answer in permanent ink, so what you know about a person sits unspent for years and then arrives on them all at once.
tension: nobody asked is the honest reply, and it is accurate — what you answered was under the request rather than in it. so the work goes out at full size onto a person who made no request and is now holding one, permanently. thanks has nowhere to attach: accepting it would mean agreeing that the thing you heard in them was there, and most people would rather carry the debt.
cost: you can sit an hour with somebody and come out knowing what it was actually about, without being told, without asking the question that would have made them decide it in words. then you act on it, and they are on the record as having meant something they never said. deniability is gone on both sides at once, and neither of you gets back to not knowing.

lead: every question you have ever asked was asked at full size, because The Drum cannot learn where it is without sending something out, and nothing you send can be taken back.
sun: a stroke is supposed to be cheap — that is the whole method, many light ones, no single one carrying much, the pattern doing the work. there is no light setting available to you. so each one lands whole and stays whole, and what should have been a pulse nobody consciously registers becomes a row of separate permanent events, every one of them dated and attributable.
moon: and the beat has no way to pause and check. tempo is the one thing that fails by stopping, so you keep going at a rate designed for something cheap while being billed for something permanent. the return never comes back clearly enough to settle whether it is wanted, and the only instrument you have for asking is another stroke.
pull: you cannot ask a small question. finding out whether anyone is out there costs them a full-size event, so you go on sending, and count the silence as an answer.
tension: the complaint, when it arrives, is about the pace and never about a particular stroke, which is why it comes without an example attached. people cannot point to the one that was too much — they can only report the accumulation, and an accumulation sounds like a mood on their side rather than a fact about you. so it gets raised as their failing, dropped, and raised again a year later by somebody else.
cost: you can hold a system's time for years, through stretches when nothing about it was rewarding, and the people inside it set their day by you without having agreed to anything. checking whether the tempo is wanted means setting it again, at cost, on somebody. every test you run leaves a permanent mark on whoever you ran it on, and the answer costs more than the question was worth.

lead: the offer was casual on their side and binding on yours. that is what The Void does when the space it opens cannot afterwards be closed — you are held to every door you have ever left open.
sun: what you open, opens for good. there is no trial period on an offer made at this size, no version where a door hangs ajar for a season and quietly goes back to shut, so the arrangement you made space for on one easy evening is load-bearing a decade later — and you are the only party to it who thinks a decision was taken that night.
moon: and an opening does not close by degrees. you cannot withdraw a quarter of it, or let it narrow across a year the way most people end things. closing is one move, full size, dated. so they accumulate, all of them live, held open for people who moved on without ever having to say so.
pull: everything you opened is open, and the day you shut one will be the only thing on your record, because a door left open has never once counted as something a person did.
tension: lucky is what you get called, and luck describes a place rather than a person — good things happened where you were, so the location took the credit and you were counted as part of it. nothing you cleared goes down as an act. then one closure lands whole, the first thing you have ever visibly done, and it goes onto the record by itself, with everything you held open nowhere near it.
cost: you can make space for a person without first working out what they will do with it, which is why things go well around you and why nobody has to earn their way in. openings do not count as events. nothing you have given anybody is written down anywhere, no one owes you for it, and the one time you take a space back is written forever.

lead: the structure everybody shelters under is standing on one support, and the support has weather. what you feel gets felt at the volume of the whole house, and no room in it is far enough away to be spared.
sun: the full-volume thing happens indoors. what leaves you leaves inside a shelter you built, so it lands on the people who have nowhere else to be that night — and they cannot step outside it, because outside it is precisely what you made them safe from. no undo keeps the night in the structure afterwards, with everyone who was standing in it when it came through.
moon: the single pole cannot step out and have the evening elsewhere. everyone inside is inside because you are standing exactly where you are standing, so nothing else is holding the roof up while you go all the way in. the whole enclosure moves with you, at your size, and the people it protects feel it through the one thing protecting them.
pull: the people you keep safe are the same people with no way of getting out of range of you, and it is one upright holding both of those facts in place.
tension: walking on eggshells is the phrase, and it gets used by people who would be sleeping somewhere considerably worse if you were not doing what you do. neither of those cancels the other out. so the wariness stops being said aloud and becomes household procedure instead — news held until a good evening, the question asked twice, the subject nobody opens, all of it arranged around a forecast nobody will admit to keeping.
cost: you can carry a household through a decade of something and never once hand any of it to the people inside; the cover does not come off because you are tired. what does not exist is anywhere to go. nothing stands over you, and the thing you are inside is standing on you, so the worst hour of your life happened in the one room you could not leave.

lead: The Chamber has no provisional setting and neither does The Storm, so what you offered as a favour was load-bearing by the second month, and nobody inside it was ever asked to agree to a room.
sun: no undo is a property of what you put up rather than of how you feel. everything goes up at full height on the first pass — no propped version, nothing tacked together to see whether the shape holds — so an arrangement made in one enthusiastic season becomes the arrangement people live inside for forty years, and taking it apart is not a smaller job than raising it was.
moon: the first wall does not ask what was standing there before. a stay becomes an address, a favour becomes a standing arrangement, a bad winter becomes a household, and this sun leaves no lighter version on the table. so the enclosing finishes before anyone registers it starting, and people learn how permanent they are to you at the exact moment they go to move.
pull: nobody has turned you down, ever, because by the time refusing was an option they were already living inside the thing you had built around them.
tension: nobody has ever accused you of giving too grudgingly. the complaint, when it finally comes, is that things with you turn real too fast — somebody meant to try something out and instead acquired a life, and the trying was over before they noticed it starting. said plainly that sounds ungrateful, so it gets said at an exit, all at once, and the years of structure underneath do not read as mitigation. they read as the charge itself.
cost: you can give a person a permanent place in your life inside a week, at full size, without having to be talked into any of it. everyone near you is standing inside something you raised around them, and nobody inside has been out of it since. their staying proves nothing you are able to use, so whether you were chosen stays a question you cannot ask anybody.

lead: one sentence of yours ended a marriage that had been dying for nine years, and it worked, and you have not seen the inside of the life that started the following morning.
sun: no undo lands on the sending. what you say about somebody's situation arrives at the size of a verdict, and a verdict does not sit quietly in a person for a season while they turn it over — they act on it that week, and the job or the country or the marriage is finished behind them. so you are permanently a party to a departure you will not be present for one hour of.
moon: the far side is exactly where your part stops. you can find the route out of things other people cannot locate the edges of, and it comes out of you whole, in a single pass, at a volume that makes the route the only visible object in the room. then the boundary. the ones you moved furthest are the ones you know least about.
pull: you can get anyone out of anything, once, permanently — and then the road is theirs, and you are standing at the edge of a country you have never entered.
tension: easy for you to say comes at you late, two years into the life you were certain about, from somebody standing in the middle of it. there is no answer available, because you were certain, and because you were not there for the winter that followed. the crossings you were right about report nothing from where you stand. the ones that went wrong report by name, at length, with dates, and they are the only post you get.
cost: you can see the way out of something a person has been drowning in for years and say it at a size that actually moves them, rather than hedging it into something nobody could act on. none of the arriving comes to you. the ones who are happy now are happy in places you have no address for, and the ones who are not have yours, and they use it.

lead: two people who have not spoken in eleven years both call you, separately, on the same night, and neither asks after the other. nothing that leaves you arrives small, including the day you stop answering.
sun: a position that exists only while it is under load has exactly one irreversible move in it, and this sun guarantees that move is enormous. everything you do to keep two ends attached is continuous and unrecorded; the single act anybody will ever be able to point at is the letting go. so the working decade is invisible and the parting is at full volume, and only one of them is on file.
moon: the cord holds at maximum because there is no lighter setting available to hold at. you take the pull from both directions for years and file it as ordinary, and neither end ever learns what the other one weighs. what neither end can be told is that you were never one of them. you are the distance between them, taken up, and holding.
pull: you are the reason two things are still touching, and the only permanent thing you will ever be seen to do is stop.
tension: the day you let go is the only day either end has a story about. before it there was nothing to describe — a thing under even tension makes no noise — so the decade reads as no effort and the release reads as a decision taken suddenly by somebody unstable. you always end up in the middle of everything gets said, as though the middle were somewhere you wandered into rather than the only ground you have stood on.
cost: you can keep two people in each other's lives who have every reason to be finished, for a decade, absorbing the pull from both directions without asking either of them to slacken. you have no inside. you exist as the space between two other people, and when they settle it, or die, nothing is left standing in the place where you were.

lead: you were there inside the first minute, before anyone had finished describing the problem, and by the time the second person arrived it had stopped being a favour and become a matter with standing.
sun: nothing you do arrives informally. the seat travels with you to the doorstep, so a hand put out at speed lands with the weight of an official visit — the room straightens, the register changes, and the person you meant to steady is now inside an arrangement rather than a kindness. they cannot wave it off afterwards, and they cannot ask for it again without asking for the whole apparatus.
moon: The Gate gets you there; the chair keeps you there. whatever you reached first is yours to preside over from then on, so the ordinary emergency you happened to be nearest becomes a standing office, and every year of answering fastest leaves you holding one more of them that nobody remembers assigning.
pull: nobody has ever received a small favour from you. what you reached first, you now preside over, and the emergency that put you in the room ended years ago.
tension: somebody wanted twenty minutes of help and left holding a permanent obligation. people who need only a hand learn from that and ask somebody lighter, so the ones still approaching are the ones who came for the weight. they are grateful and they are not friends. you make everything a production, they say, and it is said fondly, by people who would not dream of dropping in.
cost: you can walk into the worst night of a household and hold the register steady inside the first minute, so the panic organises itself around you and stops being panic. nobody does that for you. the arrival you supply on instinct is the one thing that cannot be supplied to you, because reaching you takes an appointment, and by the time anyone has one the hour has passed.

lead: there is no posture available for not yet. the chair reads a quiet month as a decision already taken, and what you are actually doing in that month is carrying something to full term with nothing to show anyone.
sun: what leaves this chair does not stay small. a preference let out once becomes the way a household or a department runs, and it goes on running that way long after anyone remembers it was a preference. so the holding lengthens. each year you keep a thing inside, you are protecting the one draft it will ever get before it hardens into somebody else's furniture.
moon: a burden that shows collects hands under it. The Bearer's never shows, and this seat advertises capacity on top of that, so the term runs its whole length with nobody offering to take an end. the timing stays yours alone, which sounds like power until you notice that the date was never negotiated with anyone, only announced.
pull: everything you have carried has been carried at full weight, in public, from a chair, by a person the room calls unbothered — and that description is the reason no hand has ever come.
tension: calculating is the charitable reading, and it credits you with a plan. the ungenerous one arrives later, from whoever waited: that you sat on something they needed while it suited you. neither account has room for the actual year, which was spent carrying an unfinished thing in a chair that makes unfinished look like a position. whichever version the room prefers is the one that goes on the record.
cost: you can hold a decision for two years inside a role that is asked about it weekly, give nothing away, and produce it at the end intact and load-bearing. nobody knows there was a choice. what you release gets received as the way things were always going to go, so the years of carrying it disappear into how obvious it looks once it is standing.

lead: the room outside has been dealing with one impeccably consistent person for decades and has never met the same one twice. The Gathered Stars take turns in a seat that holds its shape through every handover.
sun: the chair holds the commitments, not the person in it. whichever of you was sitting when a promise was made signed it in the single name you all answer to, and the next one to take the seat inherits it whole, already running, witnessed. so you keep terms you can only recall from outside, and no procedure exists for saying which of you meant them.
moon: the several would ordinarily get sorted by pressure — a hard year burns off whichever of them was never real. this seat takes the heat instead, and takes it invisibly, so nothing in you is put under enough of it to settle the question. you arrive at the far end of a long life still several, still undisputed from outside, still without a result.
pull: the steadiness everyone relies on belongs to the chair. the several who have taken turns in it are each unwitnessed, and every one of them assumes the others were the reliable one.
tension: consistency is what people praise, and they are praising a chair. at close range it stops working: anyone who stays long enough starts noticing the handover — a preference reversed, a warmth that was there last year and is not now — and because the seat presents no seam, they decide they are being handled. so every close relationship arrives at the same suspicion, and the actual reason has never been available to give.
cost: you can be relied on absolutely — the office answers when anyone knocks, in the same voice, whoever is currently in it, and that is worth more to people than a person would be. what nobody gets is a witness. every one of you has done real work, and all of it is filed under one continuous character that belongs to the chair.

lead: the seat you hold was shaped by the person you follow, and every day in it is either continuing them or correcting them. the room believes it is watching you decide.
sun: the seat takes whoever sits in it seriously, so your private argument with one absent person is conducted in public policy. a rule gets changed and forty people rearrange their week around it; none of them knows the change was addressed to somebody who left years ago and has never asked. what you are doing reads as governance and functions as correspondence.
moon: what The Follower keeps in view here has a name and a way of doing this exact job. so every choice gets tried against theirs first, privately, before anyone in the room sees it, and any departure from their method has to be argued on its own merits — the person you are actually answering cannot be named in the meeting.
pull: the room takes your rulings as yours. each one is a letter to somebody who stopped reading, sent from a chair they never sat in.
tension: you have never made it your own is what gets said, usually by someone who arrived long after you did and has no idea what they are describing. the version of you they want would require dropping the measure, and the measure is the reason the work is good. so the charge is accurate and unanswerable at once, and you take it in silence, from the front of a room that thinks the silence is confidence.
cost: you can keep a standard alive for thirty years after the person who set it stopped — hold the shape, run it better than it was run, and hand it on in working order. the credit for it is unassignable. what stands there carries somebody else's design and your whole working life, and the only person who could say which part is yours has never been asked.

lead: nobody near you has been off duty in years. the one faculty you own that needs people unguarded is aimed permanently at a room that straightened itself before you walked into it.
sun: the searching face does its best work by going first and looking foolish, and no version of you is available to look foolish. so the finding gets done at second hand — through people who report back, through reading, through the one or two allowed to watch you not know a thing. what reaches you has been sorted before it left them, and you can taste the sorting, and it is still the only supply.
moon: the appetite has no manners. you want the low, close, immediate things — who is lying, what the room smelled like, how the trick is really done — and the wanting keeps its size while the asking goes underground. so you learn by watching instead, from where you sit, and watching is slower than a question and gets you a version of the answer people have had time to prepare.
pull: you have the best seat in the room and the sharpest nose in it, and everything within range of both has been arranged for you in advance.
tension: a question from a seat is not a question. you ask what happened and the room hears an inquiry — people check their answer against the version they would want on the record, hand you that one, and go away certain they have been helpful. curious is not the word you get. thorough is, and exacting, and hard to satisfy, and the last one is accurate for a reason nobody has guessed: you are still hungry when they leave.
cost: you can walk into a field you know nothing about and be treated as its authority inside a week, which is a door most people spend a career not getting through. nobody teaches you anything after that. the corrections that would have made you good at it are held back out of respect, and the gap between the standing and the knowing widens every year you keep the seat.

lead: a sentence went into you years ago and is sitting there at the volume it came in at. the person who said it drove home that evening thinking the visit had gone well, and still thinks so.
sun: the moment a thing lands is the only moment anyone could see it land, and you spend that moment looking well. nothing gets reported, so nothing gets repaired, and the person walks away with an accurate memory of an easy conversation. what happened to you has no witness, which means it has no date, no size anyone agreed to, and no route back to the person who caused it.
moon: and none of it can be revised afterwards. the reading you took in that second is the reading — no undo works inward as well, so a person can be finished with in a single afternoon and go on being invited for another nine years, warmly, by someone who settled the matter before the coffee was cleared. they find out at the end, and there is nothing to appeal to.
pull: everything anyone has ever done to you landed whole on a face that reported nothing. the injury has no record anywhere, and nobody is carrying a debt they know about.
tension: nothing gets to you is the compliment, and it is repeated by people describing a capacity rather than a posture. the practical result is repetition: the thing that landed once goes on being done, at intervals, by someone who has had no reason to stop. and when the invitations quietly end, it lands as arbitrary — you cannot produce a wound whose only evidence would have been a change in your face a decade ago.
cost: you can take the worst news in a household and pass it on at a size people can survive, because the size they take it at is the size your face gave it. the settling is done entirely inside, where the terms are set by nobody. no one has ever had to change a habit on your account, and the changing all happens at your end, unmentioned.

lead: every reconciliation in your life was walked toward you. The Throne does not go and fetch anybody, and what comes back has to cover the whole distance itself, which is why you have never learned what the walk costs.
sun: the seat does not follow anyone out. when someone goes, the whole apparatus of you stays exactly where it was — same room, same hours, same standing invitation nobody was told about — and staying still, from a distance, is indistinguishable from being unbothered by the leaving. so the years of holding the position are invisible, and the return, when it comes, is received rather than won.
moon: what comes back arrives at a place that did not move, so the second time is always granted and never requested. you have no practice at the approach — no version of yourself standing in a doorway hoping. and because readmission is yours to give, you give it with a straight face, which the returner reads as forgiveness and files as settled, while nothing about the leaving was ever discussed.
pull: everyone who ever left you came back to the same chair, and not one of them has ever had to watch you cross a room to get them.
tension: you never came after me is the charge, and it is filed by people who came back anyway, which is what makes it unanswerable. a person keeping the door open and a person not minding look identical from any distance, and the difference lived in a room they had already left. so the return is warm and settles nothing: they arrive convinced they were not missed, and a year of waiting cannot be entered into the record now.
cost: you give people their place back without making them pay for it — no interrogation, no probation, the chair is where it was and the conversation resumes. what you have no route to is being taken back yourself. the approach requires a visible want, and yours does not show, so the one time you need the door held it will look to them like a formality you are performing.

lead: the most visible thing about you is a chair. how much of you is left by the end of a week is what The Ghost keeps off the record, and everybody has been estimating it from the furniture.
sun: what the seat implies about your supply is the only figure anyone has, and every ask gets sized to it rather than to what is actually there. the people doing the asking would not dream of taking from someone who looked short, which is the whole difficulty: they are not careless. being drawn on is simply the ordinary condition of knowing you, and nobody who does it counts it as taking.
moon: what goes out of you goes out without edges, in amounts neither side could name afterwards, so the taking never registers as an event on anyone's ledger, least of all yours. you find out the total the way everyone else does — by reaching for something ordinary and finding the place empty. a chair looks the same either way, which is why nobody checks.
pull: people take what a chair like that looks able to spare, and nobody has ever checked the estimate against the contents, and the one person who could has no gauge for it either.
tension: you don't need anything gets said as a description and works as an assignment. it was settled at family scale — the sibling who fell apart got the attention, the arrangement made sense to everyone, and you agreed with it. so the giving is never entered as generosity; it is entered as surplus, and surplus does not get thanked. people do not thank a room for being warm. they notice the day it goes cold.
cost: holding up several people at once is unremarkable to you, and none of them knows the others exist. the room stays orderly because whatever is ragged in it gets absorbed before it reaches the floor. asking is the move that goes missing. a request has to show a shortfall, and the chair answers the question of your shortfall before you have opened your mouth.

lead: one careful sentence in a corridor, eleven years ago, and a name stopped appearing on the shortlists. you have not spoken that freely since. everything you have noticed in the years after has stayed where it landed.
sun: an opinion does not leave this chair as an opinion. a hesitation you name out loud gets minuted, acted on, and remembered as a finding, so the read you took in half a second acquires the weight of a decision made slowly by a committee. the room cannot hear you thinking aloud. it only hears you ruling, and it rearranges itself accordingly before you have finished the sentence.
moon: the noticing does not stop for being unsayable. you keep a live account of everyone in the building, revised weekly, stated never. contact that holds keeps verdicts as readily as it keeps people, so a reading seals at the second it is taken, and no evidence arriving afterwards gets anywhere near it — nobody has been told there is anything to appeal.
pull: you are famously fair. the actual judgments were entered years ago, in silence, at a resolution nobody credits, and there is no procedure anywhere for getting one of them reopened.
tension: nobody has ever called you unfair, and by any measure available to them nobody could — you say nothing, you show nothing, everyone gets the same face and the same hearing. the sorting happens behind all that, on material gathered in half-seconds, and it settles who gets the interesting work for a decade. whoever it goes against feels the outcome, cannot locate the cause, decides the place is arbitrary, and stops trying.
cost: you are right about people early, and early is what makes it worth anything — you know inside a meeting and act on it for years before anyone else has cause to. from the seat the reading never gets tested. nothing obliges you to put it to the person, so the handful you got wrong have gone on running, untouched, for as long as they have been wrong.

lead: there is nothing opposite it in you. no lower setting, no room in the house where it comes off, no slouching version anywhere — the same person answers the door, the phone, and the worst news.
sun: the room stops experiencing this as something you are doing. consistency at this length gets reclassified as nature, and nature does not get thanked or relieved — nobody offers to take a turn at being the weather. so everything addressed to you comes through the formal door, because there is no informal one, and what arrives is only ever what somebody judged worth a proper approach.
moon: from inside there is no interval either. you cannot catch yourself out of it, so you hold no observation of what you would be without it, and nothing beside it to take a measurement from. tiredness arrives as information rather than sensation — noticed late, off evidence, the way you would notice it in somebody else.
pull: affection and deference reach you through the same door, in the same handwriting, at the same hour. undiluted, with nothing in you set lower, there is no test that would tell them apart.
tension: impressive is the compliment and it arrives instead of the other ones. nobody has described you as easy. at close range it turns into a request — let me see you with the guard down — and there is no guard, so the thing being asked for does not exist and cannot be produced. what you offer instead is more access to the same person, which is exactly what was already there, and the failure gets filed as withholding.
cost: a promise you made at twenty-two is executed at sixty in the identical manner, and people build their lives on that with good reason. nothing about you is ever news, though. everyone who knows you took their full reading in the first year and has updated nothing since, so you are accurately described by accounts that stopped being written decades ago.

lead: six weeks of preparation went into the twenty minutes, and the word waiting for you afterwards is natural. The Mane spreads it open and the chair keeps it level, no effort has ever made it onto the record.
sun: the seat will not let strain show, and the room reads no strain as no strain — so a thing that took everything is entered as a thing that took nothing. you get credited with a gift, which is a compliment that removes the whole of the labour from the account. nobody is being unfair. they are reading the only surface available, and it is smooth by construction.
moon: the spread makes the doing pleasant to watch, and pleasure is the enemy of credit — an audience enjoying itself is not counting anything. so the harder the week, the better the performance reads, and the better it reads, the less of it registers as work. people leave describing how easy you make it look, and they all mean it kindly.
pull: the six weeks are not in the record and the twenty minutes are. when you finally cannot do it, the only explanation anyone has left is that you stopped caring.
tension: a natural gets no allowance for a bad year. effort was never entered, so its absence is the only reading available when something goes wrong, and complacent arrives fast, from people who have watched you succeed and never watched you prepare. the charge cannot be answered by producing the preparation — hours nobody saw, described afterwards by the person who benefits, sound like an excuse assembled to fit.
cost: hard things go smoothly around you — a difficult hour with forty people in it stays comfortable, nobody feels the load, and the whole thing lands as though it were always going to. the load is priced at zero everywhere it appears. you can spend a decade doing the most demanding work in the building and arrive at the end of it with a reputation for being lucky.

lead: this is the fourth life. new city, new trade, nobody in it who knew the last one — and by the eighteenth month there is a chair in the corner of it with your shape already worn into the seat.
sun: whatever The Turning empties, the seat rebuilds. within a year of arriving anywhere you are the one people bring things to, standing at the same distance from everyone, holding the same position you left. it does not require ambition or even consent — you simply behave the way you behave, and a room organises itself around that within about nine months, every time, in every town.
moon: the molt is total and it is honest: the person who lived there is gone, not travelling under another name. what does not molt is the manner, so each emptying delivers you, clean and unaccompanied, into the identical arrangement one town over. the hope every time is that the distance was the town. it was never the town.
pull: four clean starts, four identical results. the experiment has been run enough times to have an answer, and the answer is that the distance travels with you.
tension: solid is the word now and cold is the word in the life before it, and both sets of people are describing the same fortnight. the ones you left saw a departure with nothing on its face; the ones you are among now see someone who has clearly always been here. neither group can be told about the other, because the account only makes sense laid end to end, and nobody has ever had the whole of it.
cost: ending a whole life and standing up complete in the next one inside a year is not something most people manage even once, and you have done it repeatedly. the witnesses go with each ending. the only people who could confirm any of what you have done are in towns you no longer enter, and nothing accumulates under one name.

lead: a suggestion you made in passing is now a department. nobody in the room could have told you it was a poor idea, and by the time it had a budget you had forgotten saying it.
sun: the chair converts an impulse into an instruction somewhere between your mouth and the door. what you offered as a thought to kick around comes back six weeks later built, staffed, and defended by people who took your hesitating aloud for a test of their nerve. so nothing you start is ever weighed by anyone before it is standing, and the weighing was the part you needed.
moon: the maker's hand cannot tell a thing that moved because it was good from a thing that moved because of where it came from, and nothing in this arrangement separates them. so the talent runs at full stretch on evidence it cannot read. what you have started is enormous, and none of it has been tried against a room that was free to decline.
pull: every idea of yours has been agreed to. the good ones and the bad ones came back built, on schedule, by people with no way of telling you which was which.
tension: visionary gets said without warmth — it is what people call a person whose half-formed notions they have spent a decade executing. when one of them fails, the room produces its reservations all at once, fully formed, dated to the week you first mentioned it. they are not lying. the chair is what kept them quiet, and pointing at the chair from the chair is not a move available to you.
cost: you can put a thing into the world in one sentence and it exists — most people spend years on the gap between saying and standing, and you have never met the gap. what has never happened is a correction. the room's judgement runs downstream of yours, so the only thing that has ever stopped an idea of yours is the idea itself, at scale, after it was built.

lead: you have been alone in every fight, and the reason is architectural. what the seat looks like from outside is backing, so everyone who might have stood in front of you has read it and gone back to work.
sun: standing does two things to an undefended person, and protection is not either of them. it lifts what you make into the sightline of people who have no stake in it, and it tells everyone watching that you have recourse — a lawyer, an ally, an arrangement, something. none of those exists. so what arrives is sized to the position, and what receives it is a person at a table.
moon: the position comes with instruments — a door you could close, a name you could withhold, a cost you could impose on someone exactly once — and The Jewel has never had one in its hand. people establish this within a season. after that the standing deters nothing; it advertises. what is loaded belongs to the chair, and your conduct has told everybody it will not be lifted.
pull: the safest-looking place in the room, occupied by the one person in it holding nothing. everybody worked that out years ago, and nobody has mentioned it to you.
tension: the one time you use the position to stop something, it will not read as a person defending their work. from that height any refusal is punishment, and the room measures it against the fifteen years you spent refusing nothing. so the first no is the cruel one, and the story about it outlives the thing you were protecting. gracious gets said until then, and it names what you have not done.
cost: you keep working undefended at a height where everyone else has hired protection, so what you make has no committee in it and people can feel that from across a room. the absorbing has no end and no name: a person at your level is assumed to have someone who handles this, and you are the person who handles it.

lead: thirty people organise their week around where you will be sitting. not one of them has ever been told that you could stand up tomorrow and lose nothing you would miss.
sun: the chair assigns you a people. everyone who comes through it reads the position as a pledge — that you are of this — and the reading is never spoken aloud, so it is never checked. year by year the place builds itself around a member it does not have. you are given the loyalty owed to one and asked for the loyalty owed by one, and only the first half has ever arrived.
