moon: The Veil decided nothing here; standing apart arrived as a fact, leaving no date on it and nothing to confess. the chair then does the covering: people read a position and stop reading, satisfied, because occupancy looks like belonging from every angle they have. you conceal nothing. you are the one fact about the place nobody has thought to check, and saying it aloud would land as a resignation.
pull: you hold the middle of a thing you never joined. they would call it mutual, and what they would be describing is a chair that has not moved.
tension: the leaving is the part that gets remembered. one day the position ends and it turns out nothing tore, and the room rereads the whole tenure backwards from that: never really in it, halfway gone the entire time. it was all real. it was simply never membership. explaining the difference requires saying out loud that their belonging and your presence were two separate things, which is worse than the charge, so the charge stands.
cost: you are the only person in the building without a side, so your judgements come out clean and everyone knows it, which is why the position keeps being handed back to you. thirty people are loyal to someone with no stake in them, nobody has noticed, and the debt runs one direction with no currency available for the other.

lead: a chair speaks once and in one direction. The Claws arrive at every question carrying both answers whole, and one of them has never been let out of the room.
sun: the position has a single voice and it issues findings. whichever half reaches your mouth first leaves as a ruling, and the room does not wait — by the afternoon there are schedules built on it, and the other half, which you still hold entire, is now underneath a structure. reversing it later costs more than being wrong costs, so you go on being right about the half you said.
moon: from inside, nothing was chosen. the branch that got spoken is not the truer one, and the one underneath goes on working at the same strength, which is why the most persistent objection to your policy is yours. you slow it, you make exceptions, you protect the people it was going to cost — quietly, from the office that wrote it — and the room cannot account for the drag.
pull: every decision on your record is half of what you thought, delivered in a voice that admits no halves, and the missing half has been quietly working against it ever since.
tension: decisive is what the room settled on years ago, and the people closest to the work have a second word they do not say in front of the first. when the buried half finally has to be acted on, it arrives as a reversal — someone who changed their mind, not someone who held both from the start. no record of the second half exists anywhere, because a seat has no venue for thinking out loud.
cost: you can take a question with two right answers and hand the room one instruction it can act on that morning, which is why the position works. the half you did not say is not admissible later. when the thing goes wrong in exactly the way you privately expected, the expectation has no standing — your name is on the other answer, in one voice, with nothing beside it.

lead: at some point in the first ten minutes the other person worked out that a refusal would have to be delivered to the chair, and after that whatever they said was going to be yes.
sun: a no has to be handed to the seat, not to you, and nobody has ever found a light way to do that. so the yes you get is real and it is also the easier of the two acts available in the room, and no test exists that separates those. every long arrangement of your life was signed in that condition, and none of the signing can be repeated now on fairer ground.
moon: a bond The Crown makes never comes up for review, so the condition it was entered under runs its whole length unexamined. and leaving you is a public act — the walking away happens in front of everybody, with the seat still standing there looking reasonable — so people stay years past the point, and call it loyalty, because loyalty is the only name the room has for staying.
pull: everyone who ever chose you was choosing in front of a chair, and all of them stayed, and neither fact has ever been separable from the other.
tension: devoted comes back about both of you at once, and that is the failure: a free choice and a refusal too costly to deliver, filed under one word. when someone finally does go, the account they give has nothing to do with you — it runs on the years it took to work out that leaving had been permitted all along, and you are the last person who could have told them that, having never had to find it out.
cost: the oaths you are inside outlast the people in them — a thing agreed with you at thirty runs at sixty in the shape it was given, and households have been built on that. whether any of it was freely entered never gets settled. you have been kept by everyone and chosen by nobody, and the decades are served now, with nothing left that would tell the two apart.

lead: two kinds of standing, one of them handed to you by a structure and one of them earned by having been present, and the room has never had to say out loud which of the two it is obeying.
sun: the seat argues from nothing. occupancy is the whole of its case, and a room concedes it in the first week, so the thirty years never have to be entered anywhere and never are. what you know from having been there for all of it disappears into a standing you would have had on the day you arrived. the deference coming back is identical either way, which is what makes it useless to you.
moon: The Heart argues from a date. you were there, you saw it happen, and the eldest can be checked by anyone — which is what the position renders unnecessary. the two halves make one demand on incompatible ground, and when you are pushed, whichever ground you stand on the pushing moves to the other: the post does not make you right, the years do not make you the post.
pull: two claims on the same obedience, and every time you use one of them out loud you have conceded that the other one was not enough.
tension: entitled arrives eventually, and it is a poor word for someone who has never established either claim to their own satisfaction. what people are reacting to is the doubling: refuse them on one ground and they appeal on the other, so nothing you decide gets overturned and nothing gets agreed to either. they stop arguing rather than concede. after enough years the silence and the settled question are indistinguishable, and you have come to prefer the silence.
cost: a challenge to your standing has to beat two things, and almost nothing does, so you can hold a room through the year that should have taken it from you. when the position goes to someone else you find out in public, on a single afternoon, which of the two was ever yours. the decades before that were spent assuming an answer, and assuming was all that was on offer.

lead: the brake on this kind of digging was never inside The Root — it was always a person in the room saying that is enough now. from the chair, that person works for you, and they hand you the shovel.
sun: a look from the chair comes with people, hours and access, so what would have been a private curiosity arrives as a project, and the ones whose arrangement is being opened are the ones assigned to open it. they do it well. nobody can say that a thing is fine and be believed, because the asking has already established that it might not be, and the asking came from the front.
moon: the sentence that ends a dig — enough now, put it back — has to be said upward here, and the people positioned to say it decided against that years ago. what you take apart does not go back together. a structure opened this far from that height has been ruled on, and nobody rebuilds against a ruling; they file it and move to whatever you look at next.
pull: nothing you ever wondered about has survived the wondering, and every hand that took it apart with you belonged to somebody who lived in it.
tension: everything here has been opened except the arrangement that authorises the opening, and people keep count. you can dig into anything handed to you; you cannot commission a dig into your own standing, because there is nobody to hand it to and doing it yourself returns the answer you wanted. the charge, when it arrives, comes from someone already leaving, and checking it is the one piece of work you cannot assign to anybody.
cost: you find what a thing is actually standing on and you can act on it that week, so the hollow beam leaves the building before it comes down on anyone. nothing gets left alone. the marriage, the arrangement you were not worried about, your own account of your childhood — each got the identical treatment at the identical depth, and each came apart on schedule.

lead: you passed over one item on a crowded morning, without deciding anything about it, and nobody has put it in front of you since — not the person whose it was, not anyone.
sun: attention from the chair is the only currency the place has, and you spend it without noticing, which means you withdraw it without noticing. a topic you did not get to is read as weighed and set down, and the reading never gets checked with you, because checking would mean asking whether you meant it, and nobody asks the chair what it meant. the discard needs no act from you.
moon: The Flock sorts by leaving things behind, a light action for you and a permanent one for everybody else: you set it down, refill, and go on, and the year the group spends without it never reaches you. what you dropped belonged to somebody — a way of doing the work, an arrangement, an hour in the week — and none of it was yours to be light about.
pull: nothing you set down has ever been picked back up. half of it you never decided to drop, and everyone who lost something that way is certain you chose to.
tension: the place becomes a room of people reading your silences, and they get good at it — better than you are at producing them, since half of what they read is a busy fortnight. proposals stop coming. nobody wants the answer that arrives as no answer, so they watch what you pick up and bring more of that. focused is the admiring word for it. what you get is a place that has stopped having ideas.
cost: a crowded, deadlocked hour with nine items in it comes out of you with two, and they are the right two, and the place moves for the first time in a year — which is why the rooms keep being handed to you. the other seven do not go back to their owners. each was somebody's, and each is still waiting, quietly, to be told what happened to it.

lead: nobody has ever turned you down. an open hour offered from a seat lands as a posting rather than an invitation, and postings get accepted, so the record is spotless and tells you nothing about who wanted to come.
sun: the room you keep clear is not read as clear. anything you leave open from where you sit gets taken for a place that was prepared, so people arrive already assigned to it, already grateful, already behaving as though terms exist. what you meant as space with nothing in it comes back to you furnished with obligations you did not set out, and enforced by people who assume you did.
moon: the blank is genuine — you hold it open for whatever a person turns up with, unshaped, and you would hold it for a refusal too. no refusal comes. so the one instrument that would tell you whether the room is wanted has never been used, and you go on clearing at a width nobody has had to justify wanting.
pull: every door you have ever opened was walked through. from that chair an offer is a placement, so the yes you keep getting has never once been a yes to you.
tension: generous is what gets said, and it describes a facility more than a person. after a lifetime without a single refusal you cannot tell the guest who wanted the evening from the one who read the invitation as a fixture on the calendar, and both come, warmly, for years. the day you ask for something back, the request lands on people who were never given a chance to decline.
cost: you can hold a space open for somebody through the worst year of their life without shaping it and without asking what it is for, and the height it comes from keeps it free of obligation. nothing of yours ever goes in there. the moment something does, the room acquires a purpose and stops being room, so the width is only yours while it is holding somebody else's year.

lead: the meeting ran clean and everybody left satisfied, and nobody but you is carrying what was actually being negotiated in it, and no version of you can say so out loud.
sun: the room speaks toward the chair in a prepared voice, and it prepares well — people rehearse in the car on the way in. the unprepared sentence keeps arriving underneath anyway, and you take delivery of both. one of them was addressed to you. acting on the other would mean admitting to a channel nobody opened for you, which from the chair reads as surveillance rather than attention.
moon: the ear does not consent to any of this. it takes in the tremor under a fine report whether or not you can use what it hands you, so the accurate reading arrives, complete, several months before anything in the open would justify acting on it. you act anyway, sideways — a rota changed, a project moved — and the reasons you give are all second-best and all true.
pull: you have been told the truth about your building for thirty years by people who never said any of it, and every repair you made had to be given a different reason.
tension: unpredictable is the reputation, and the people who hold it are not careless — they can see a decision arrive without a cause attached, and a cause attached that does not fit the decision, so they settle on favouritism as the only account left. what you actually had was half a second in somebody's voice, and putting that on the table would finish the person it came from.
cost: you can defuse a thing in its second week, before anyone else has a name for it, and the building goes on believing it never had a problem. a prevented event leaves no trace to be credited with. so the record shows a run of years in which nothing much happened under you, which is the exact shape of the work.

lead: The Drum keeps time for a building that has no say in the matter, and the seat is why nobody raises it — a pace issued from that height is not a suggestion anyone tests.
sun: whatever rate you are running at becomes the rate. a slow fortnight is adopted by everyone within a week of your having it, and a hard push is matched the same way, so the place runs at the speed of one body, and does it obediently in both directions. nobody experiences this as compliance. they experience it as the natural speed of the work, and defend it.
moon: a return only tells you something if it was not sent by you. what comes back off a room arranged around the chair is your own count, tidied, on time, agreeing — so the instrument reports nothing and reads as confirmation. you go on setting a tempo you have no way of checking, and the better the place performs it, the less you learn.
pull: the count comes back perfect every time because you sent it. forty people are matching a pace that was never tested, and their matching it is the only test you have.
tension: a rest cannot be taken privately. an ordinary flat month travels outward as evidence about the position rather than a person, and by the third week people are revising their plans for the year on the strength of how you looked at one meeting. you push instead, the place pushes harder than you meant, and the exhaustion that follows is filed under everybody's own ambition.
cost: you can hold an operation's timing in your own body for a decade, and nobody has ever had to be told when to begin. the pace stays fitted to you rather than to the work. so a thing that needed eleven months gets nine because that is what you had in you, and it goes out on time, and being on time is what everybody remembers about it.

lead: fourteen along from the seat, directly across it, is where the full moon nearest your birthday comes up. The Void is what sits there, facing the most furnished thing you own, at exactly its width.
sun: the chair only knows how to take a thing on formally. a promise made from it gets recorded, resourced and given a review date, so what people receive from you is an arrangement with a shape they can point to, and they take that as the whole of what was agreed. the shape is accurate. it is also the smaller half, and the half with an end date on it.
moon: what you actually gave them is not on that paper. the opening took the whole person in, unfiled, with no term attached and no clause for ending it, and it holds. so you go on being bound to people whose formal claim on you lapsed years ago — a household you left, a role that ended, someone who released you in writing and does not know you did not go.
pull: they were released from you on the day the paperwork said so. you were not, and the undertaking they never knew about is the one that has been running the whole time.
tension: nothing you are carrying can be produced. the obligations everyone can see were discharged on schedule, so from outside the account is settled, and you read as someone with an unusual number of past attachments and no live ones. the people at the other end feel a warmth coming off a finished arrangement and cannot place it. some find it a burden. all of them assume you moved on when they did.
cost: you keep faith past the end of the arrangement that made it — no renewal, no contact, nobody checking — and what you undertook goes on being true while the other person's life reorganises around not knowing it. none of it is collectable. an obligation nobody entered cannot be called in, or thanked, or closed, and the one who holds the other end has nothing to hold.

lead: there is a compartment nobody with a key to the building has been shown. The Hideaway keeps four people dry in there, and none of the four knows the cover is a post somebody could take away.
sun: the position is what the cover is fixed to. the arrangement stays dry exactly as long as you keep your footing in public, and a bad quarter of yours is felt by people who have never been told they are downstream of your standing. stepping down would be a private decision with a household inside it, and the household has no representation in the room where that gets discussed.
moon: The Hideaway keeps its contents from everyone, the occupants first of all. nobody under the cover has been told what holding it takes, which is the single fact that would let one of them take a turn. so you live inside your own construction, and any offer of help that reaches you would have to arrive with no information behind it.
pull: the room has decided there is something in there worth having. what is in there is people, and they have no idea they are being kept.
tension: a closed room at your height gets read as an arrangement rather than a mercy. people go looking, and not out of malice — the position invites an audit and you have declined one. guarded is what gets said to your face; the blunter accounts run lower down, and every one could be answered in a sentence you will not say, because saying it puts four names into a conversation they have stayed out of for years.
cost: keeping people housed for years without their carrying the knowledge of it is rare, and you do it with no strain showing and no word to them. everything else you have built was made to stand on its own. the single pole under this one is a chair, and the day the chair goes, the people under it will call it bad luck.

lead: the newcomers assume the place was here before you. it very nearly wasn't — you set the first wall yourself, in a bad year, with two people — and from where you now sit that sentence cannot be said aloud.
sun: occupancy reads as prior. a person in a seat that solid gets taken for the current holder of something old, so the deference arriving at your desk is addressed to the institution and merely delivered to you. it is warm, it is real, and it will go on arriving at that desk after you leave it. nothing in the arrangement has a field for the person who put the desk there.
moon: The Chamber would not mention it to a room this friendly. you built the thing to hold without supervision and it does — it ran through the worst eighteen months you have had while you were barely there — so the proof of the work and its erasure are one fact. a claim would have to be made out loud, by you, to people who consider the question settled.
pull: you are the reason there is a room here. the room is the reason nobody can hear you say so — from that chair, authorship comes out sounding like a request to be thanked.
tension: you walked into a good situation is the account, and it is given kindly, usually by someone explaining you to a newer arrival. the people who were there for the first three years have retired, and nobody took their testimony. so proposals to change the place arrive as though the place were nobody's, and refusing one casts you as defending an inheritance — a reading you would have to accept in order to argue at all.
cost: you can put up something that holds people who will never think about it, and hand it over running, on settings you chose in a year nobody remembers. the record has one column and it says occupant. whoever comes next inherits your work under their own name, correctly, because by then that is what the place is, and the difference stopped being visible years ago.

lead: the people who have been beside you for ten years are, every one of them, people you could not place anywhere else — and the length of their service is what the room calls devotion.
sun: a sentence from this chair carries somebody across in one move. what a person could not have argued for in three years of trying, you settle with a phone call, and the placement holds because of where it came from — nobody unpicks an arrangement made at that height. so the crossing is clean, and it is also final: they cannot come partway back to test it, because returning would mean overturning you.
moon: The Guide finds the route for anyone standing in the office, and the good ones are gone within two years of finding it. what stays is whatever could not be moved — the one with a sick parent, the one nobody else wants, the one already placed once who came apart. the seat then fills up with them, and from outside that looks like a following.
pull: everyone you were any use to is somewhere else now. the room you hold is the sediment — the ones the road would not take — and its steadiness gets called loyalty.
tension: the ones who stayed have worked out what staying means, and the subject is closed in both directions. you cannot reassure someone that they were kept rather than left; the reassurance is the confirmation. so a particular quiet settles over the long-serving, and to a visitor it reads as a settled team. the word from outside is generous — careers get made here — and the people it was made for are all in other cities.
cost: you can end a person's stuck decade with one call and make it stick, which is worth more than a year of anybody's encouragement. everyone still close to you is close because the call never worked for them. the intimacy in your life is built out of your failures, and each one of them knows it, and stays.

lead: what you meant as a stopgap has been carrying traffic for twenty years. nothing issued from that seat stays temporary, so a line thrown across one bad winter is now how the two halves reach each other.
sun: the chair converts a favour into a fixture. the connection got made at that height, so nobody asked how it was being held, and within two years it was on the plans as though there were engineering under it. the load is still coming out of one body, unrecorded, and no budget exists for keeping it up, because the place has classed it as a standing feature rather than a thing somebody is doing.
moon: The Thread cannot go slack for an afternoon to see what happens, because what happens is that two ends move further apart while it is slack. so the pull gets taken continuously, in both directions, by a person who is also required to appear untouched by it, and each end increases what it asks in the belief that it is leaning on a structure.
pull: two halves of the place have been holding opposite ends of one person for twenty years. there are no drawings, and nothing about it can be handed to anybody.
tension: indispensable gets said with an edge on it, because nobody enjoys finding out that an arrangement they rely on is a person's arm. so it gets tested — a week you take, a meeting you miss — and the wobble that follows is read as proof that you have arranged things to make yourself necessary. describing the actual work from your position would sound like a claim on the record, so the testing goes on and the explanation stays unavailable.
cost: you can keep two halves of something attached across a gap nobody else can stand in, for decades, while both sides plan as though the ground between them were solid. the work cannot be taught to anybody. a cord like this is held with a particular history in a particular pair of hands — no candidate, no brief, no month of shadowing, and the post exists nowhere except in you.

lead: The Drum sets the beat in the open. The Follower keeps the pursuit out of sight. everyone around you runs on a tempo you took off a person none of them has met.
sun: the beat lands on everyone in range, and it is calibrated somewhere else. you set the pace off a standard chosen once and never renegotiated since, then hand it out as though it started with you. when the gap widens you quicken, and everyone quickens with you, and nobody can ask what changed, because what you measure against has never been in the building.
moon: the pursuit asks its question of someone who will never be in the room to answer it. so the room answers instead, warmly, on time, and none of it lands. what you keep is the shortfall, dated, itemised, running years back, and the people who set their watches by you have never been shown that it exists.
pull: everyone here runs on your count. you run on a count taken off someone who has never turned around to check that you are still there.
tension: steady is what you get called, and steady is what people call a thing they have stopped watching. you are on time and behind in the same hour, and only one of those shows. praise for the tempo arrives on schedule and lands on a version of you that is, by your own count, short, so you take it and it converts to nothing on the way in. correcting that would mean naming the standard out loud.
cost: you are unusually good at holding a pace for other people over years, through stretches when there was no reason left to hold it. the count you run against has no finish written into it, so the work lands on time forever and never lands as enough, and nobody offers to take a turn, because a beat that has not dropped does not look like weight.

lead: the offer you made in a hurry, once, to somebody in trouble, has not been withdrawn in eleven years. neither has any of the others. arriving takes a minute and the room takes a life.
sun: what you open at speed does not come with a term. an arrival is a matter of minutes; the room it leaves behind runs for decades on your side and nobody else's, because the person you reached had a crisis and you had an opening, and only one of the two ends. so the arrivals accumulate as vacancies, each one kept warm for somebody whose emergency finished years ago.
moon: the first minute is the whole of what this moon supplies, and it goes on supplying it — a new one every few weeks, at speed, into a life where the previous ones are all open. nobody is going to take one off you. what arrives first tends to belong to whoever arrived, and no second person is coming, only the same one going again.
pull: you have arrived first at everything and finished with none of it. the door you came through that fast is the same door you have been holding open ever since, unpaid, for people who left.
tension: the charge is that you never finish anything, and whoever brings it dates the failure to the week you stopped appearing. what happened is the opposite of stopping — the thing is open, the place is kept, the offer from that night has never been revoked, and none of that is visible at any distance. an arrangement nobody closed looks identical to one that was dropped, and telling the two apart requires standing exactly where you stand.
cost: you reach people inside the hour, and the place you make for them stays made — no probation, no review, nobody has to come back and requalify. none of it closes. every arrangement you ever opened is open at full width, and the ones who came at speed came once, so what you are holding is forty rooms for forty nights that ended years ago.

lead: everyone who arrives at your place finds room in it. what The Bearer is carrying has nowhere to go, because the only opening with your name on it is the one everybody else uses.
sun: room is the one thing you can produce on demand, and producing it is how you are read. an available person is assumed to be an unloaded one — the two get counted as a single fact — so the space you clear for other people works as a statement about your own contents, made in public, hourly, by you, and wrong.
moon: a thing carried this long has to come out somewhere, and the only opening you own is already in use. so the term extends. you hold while the room fills nightly with other people's business, and setting yours down in the middle of theirs would not read as a delivery — it would read as the space closing, which nobody here has ever seen you do.
pull: you are the most available person anyone knows and the fullest, and the availability is the exact reason the question of what you are carrying has never come up.
tension: low maintenance is the phrase, said affectionately, and it works as a reason to bring you more. the people saying it have watched you accommodate for years and drawn the only available conclusion, which is that accommodation is cheap for you. it is not, and the evidence would be a full term of something set on the table mid-sentence, in a room they came to for their own reasons. so the phrase goes unchallenged, and the bringing continues.
cost: there is never a bad night to arrive at your place, which is rarer than the people using it understand — no timing to check, no read on your week required before they start. the interior work runs to term regardless, unattended, and the day it finishes, whatever comes out has to be introduced to people who had no idea a second thing was in the building.

lead: room enough for all of you, which is why none of you has ever had to win. six people could describe you accurately, and each of the six would be describing somebody who made space for them.
sun: a space takes its shape from whoever is standing in it, and that is the entire disguise. whichever of you is out shapes to the visitor, who leaves having met somebody who fit, and files the fit as your character. nothing in your arrangement pushes back hard enough to make the difference between two of you into an event. the several go unsorted, comfortably, for decades.
moon: each of you keeps a different set of people, and the sets do not overlap — the ones who come for the quiet one have never met the one who talks, because the room only ever holds the party currently in it. so the several are witnessed separately and never at the same table. when somebody stops coming, one of you loses the only witness that version ever had.
pull: there was always room enough to avoid deciding. so all of you are intact and unproven, each with its own witnesses, and those witnesses have never been in one room.
tension: you agree with whoever you are with — that is the account, usually from two people comparing notes after an evening. neither of them is describing agreement. the one they met meant it, and the one the other met also meant it, and there was room for both because you have never made anybody share the floor. proving that requires putting two of them in front of the same version of you, which the room is built to prevent.
cost: you can give six people the exact size of room each of them needed, and mean it every time, with no performance in any of it. nothing has ever come back hard enough to say which of you it was aimed at. so the question of which one is real goes to the end unanswered, in a life you built to have nothing in it that could answer.

lead: stepping back and making room are one movement, and you have been doing it since you were nineteen. what everybody else sees is the room. the other half of the motion keeps the distance exactly where it was.
sun: what you clear does not sit unassigned. an opening made in front of somebody already ahead of you goes to them — more width, more air, more of whatever they were doing — and it arrives looking like courtesy rather than like fuel. so the gap you keep is funded by the same gesture everyone thanks you for, and no one watching has ever had cause to separate the two.
moon: the pursuit needs the gap held at one width, and nothing in you takes ground, so it holds — for decades, without a single conversation about it. and the front stays open the whole time. anyone could walk into it, including you, which is the part that makes the arrangement yours: the position was available every year and declined every year, quietly, by the person who cleared it.
pull: the person in front of you has had more room than anyone alive, and you are the one who kept clearing it, and the word for that, on both sides, has always been generosity.
tension: modest gets said about you, and the word describes somebody with no wants. you have one. it has held at a fixed width for thirty years and nothing else in you comes near its size, and nobody has been placed to notice, because wanting shows up in people as taking, and taking is the one behaviour you have never produced. so the description holds, and what it is wrong about goes on underneath it, undisturbed.
cost: people get larger around you. you hand over the width and they grow into it, and neither side mentions the handing. what went out is unrecoverable. it went to someone already ahead, so every year of it is a year the gap got wider, and the gesture that widened it is the one thing about you nobody has ever objected to.

lead: you have never chased anything in your life. the searching face here does its hunting by clearing a place and letting the thing walk in, which works, and which is why nothing you found has ever left.
sun: making room is how you get at anything. you do not go and take a subject, you clear a place beside you where it can be, and it arrives on its own — people, trades, whole fields, none of them pursued, all of them somehow yours. the arrangement holds afterwards. what walks into a space you opened is attached to you from then on, whether or not you are attached back.
moon: the interest ends where the answer does. you had it in the second month and the third month was another scent entirely, and none of that reached the room, which stays open, exactly as wide, holding a place for a question you finished thinking about years ago. the person in it is not mistaken about being welcome. they are only mistaken about being thought of.
pull: the room is genuinely theirs and has been for nine years. it was opened by somebody who wanted to know one thing, found it out, and has not been back inside since.
tension: flaky does not fit and gets used anyway, because the evidence for it is thin — you never withdrew anything, never took a place back, never gave anyone a date. what people are actually describing is being kept. they have standing with you and no traffic. the invitation renews itself annually without a single conversation behind it, and nobody can ask whether the host remembers why it was issued.
cost: nothing has to justify itself to get in. somebody with no credentials, a subject with no use — you have room, so it gets room, and half of what you know arrived that way. the accounts stay open forever. you are carrying a standing obligation to everything that ever interested you for a fortnight, and no method for telling which of them you want now.

lead: there was never a wall for it to hit. what you felt at twenty-three crossed the whole distance at the size it started, landed intact on somebody, and has been on the record ever since.
sun: the opening does not push back. every capacity you have for accommodating a thing is available at once, which means nothing internal ever tells you the size of what is happening — no strain, no crowding, no point where a feeling meets the edge of what you can hold and reports its dimensions to you. you find out how large it was from the damage, or from someone's face, months on.
moon: no undo needs a wall to be survivable. everyone else runs up against the end of what they can hold and gets stopped there, half-delivered, which is the mechanism that spares them most of what they nearly did. yours goes out whole instead — at the size it had inside you, into a room that offered no resistance and gave no sign that any was called for.
pull: everyone else is saved by running out. nothing in you runs out, so the worst of it arrived at the far end complete, and there was nothing in between to take the edge off.
tension: intense is the word that comes back, and it arrives without an incident attached, which makes it impossible to answer. there was no moment where you overran anything — the room kept taking it. so the correction everyone else gets in their twenties, the one delivered by hitting a limit in front of witnesses and being embarrassed, never happened here, and what people are reacting to is a grown person operating without it.
cost: a person can put the whole thing in front of you at its real size and watch it be taken seriously — no flinch, no rationing, no visible effort at keeping up. what they set down stays at that weight on your side, permanently, while theirs shrinks to the size a normal memory keeps. they get the relief. you get the original.

lead: a homecoming needs a shut door. The Void has never shut one, so the people who left keep wandering back in on ordinary evenings, and the reunion you were owed never gets its occasion.
sun: you keep the place set. nobody gets removed from the list, no seat is reassigned, the door stands where it stood — meant as fidelity, received as no information at all. a person cannot tell from an open door whether they were missed, because it looks identical to an open door nobody was thinking about. so the holding is real and unreadable, and it costs the one being held exactly nothing to ignore.
moon: what comes back needs to have gone, and nothing here is permitted to go. so the second time never arrives as a second time. they resume, mid-sentence, eight years on, and it is warm and easy and undramatic, and the part you were built to feel — the door opening, the returning — has nowhere to attach. you wait for arrivals that have been happening in the doorway all along.
pull: nobody has ever come back to you, because nobody was ever able to leave. eight years of silence ends with a text about a restaurant, and that is the whole reunion.
tension: you are the one everybody can come back to, and the phrase people use is no hard feelings, which is a compliment about you and a description of a facility. nobody has to make an approach, so nobody makes one. the apology that would have been owed to a closed door goes unspoken because the door was open, and years of it accumulate as an unpaid amount that cannot be itemised, since no single evening did anything wrong.
cost: people who have burned every other bridge arrive at yours intact, with nothing withheld on re-entry and nothing to be re-earned. the door being open is why nobody has ever registered a door at all. you have been forgiving continuously for thirty years, in advance, on people who never found out, and the whole of it reads as nothing having happened.

lead: the friendship ended in its ninth year because she was finished, and the news reached you as news. nothing on your side was ever going to say when — the space had not filled, the supply had not run down.
sun: room is the resting state here, not a thing you decide to make. the space is already open when the request arrives, which removes the moment at which a refusal would have been possible — you are not saying yes to anything. nothing has ever reached you in a form that could be answered, and a person who is never asked never grows the part that declines.
moon: the haze that feeds carries no gauge either. what leaves you is unmeasured at both ends, and a thing with no edges gives no signal of running low — it thins evenly, everywhere, which arrives as ordinary tiredness and gets handled as ordinary tiredness. the number shows up the first time something structural gives way, by which point the number is history.
pull: you have never ended anything. every finish in your life was somebody else reaching their limit, and the limit was theirs because you have never located one of your own.
tension: selfless comes up, and generous, and neither is being used as praise so much as description, the way people describe a climate. a person with no stopping point cannot be wronged in any way that shows. nobody took too much, because too much requires a line, and the ones closest in have been drawing on you for a decade without a single moment either of you could point at.
cost: anyone can take what they need from you without having to prove they need it, which is rare enough that people arrange their lives to be near it. none of it can be paid back. returning a thing requires knowing how much it was, and the amount was never established at either end, so what you get instead of gratitude is fondness, indefinitely, at no particular rate.

lead: people take their guard off in your company without deciding to, because an opening does not read as an audience. The Glance is running the whole time, and nothing it takes in ever leaves.
sun: an open space reads as unwatched even with you standing in it. whatever makes room in you also takes away the last cue people use to notice they are being observed, so they put their material down in front of you as they would put it down alone — the difficult sentence about their marriage, the flinch at a certain name. what makes them careless is the room, and the room is you.
moon: nothing was handed to you, which is the part that makes it permanent. a confidence has a shape — it can be repeated, or returned, or brought up years later by either person. what you have instead is the unedited version of everybody, taken at the resolution it happened at, filed under nothing, with no second party who knows the file exists.
pull: everyone relaxes in an open room. you are the room, and thirty years of what people did while they thought nothing was watching sits in you at full resolution and cannot be raised.
tension: easy to talk to is the standing description, and it is issued by people who have told you things they have told nobody else and do not remember doing it. the discomfort is one-sided and has no incident in it. you know which of two friends went cold first, by nine months, and you cannot say so, because saying it would identify you as somebody who was counting the whole time in a room that advertised the opposite.
cost: people arrive at you already off-duty, and they get a genuine hour of not being read — no follow-up questions, no visible interest, no sign that anything registered. it registered. the record is exact and it is yours alone to keep, so the friendliest room anybody has is maintained by the one person in it who has never been off-duty.

lead: fourteen mansions along, at the far end of the line that runs through you, sits The Throne — the full moon closest to your birthday rises there. what stands opposite an opening is a chair with a posture.
sun: the invitation is unconditional and it is real. nobody has to arrive in any particular condition, nothing has to be brought, no version of themselves has to be assembled on the way over — you clear the ground and mean every inch of it. that is the first of two instructions you give simultaneously, and the only one you can hear yourself giving.
moon: the second one goes out through your bearing, which was on before you entered and takes no direction from you. people read carriage faster than words. so they cross a threshold that promised nothing would be required and meet a person who is visibly not slouching, and they adjust — coats stay on longer, the swearing thins out, and the evening becomes a good one rather than an easy one.
pull: you built the one place where nobody has to perform, and you are standing in it, and the standing is what they perform for.
tension: dignified is what you get called, warmly, by people who did not fully let go in your company. they leave your table having had a fine evening and go on somewhere lesser for the sloppy one. neither half of you is doing anything wrong. a total welcome delivered by somebody with that much carriage asks a guest to relax at attention, and no guest has ever found a way to lodge that as a complaint.
cost: the worst people bring their worst to you and behave well doing it — the room takes them, the bearing sets the terms, and nothing has to be enforced by anyone. best behaviour is what you have on record. you have never seen the version of your closest people that comes out at two in the morning in somebody else's kitchen.

lead: halfway across the room they have decided what you will give them. what The Mane advertises from that far off is abundance. what is here is width — a place to be, not what anyone set out for.
sun: the only thing you can hand anybody is room, and you hand it fast and ask nothing for it. somebody sits down loaded with a decision and gets an afternoon with nothing in it except them — no verdict, no contact, no loan, no plan. that is the whole of what you have, it never runs down, and it reaches them long after they have started accepting something else.
moon: the display runs whether or not there is anything behind it to display, and it cannot be turned down for honesty's sake — a mane is not a decision. so the promise goes out ahead of you into every room, permanently, at a size you did not set: more resource, more answer, more of whatever the person is short of. and then they get here.
pull: they came for a full thing and were given somewhere to stand. the ones who understand what happened never leave, and the rest go away vaguely unpaid.
tension: the word that comes off people afterwards is disappointing, and almost nobody says it out loud, because nothing was withheld and nothing was promised in language. you overpromise by existing. the correction is unavailable to you — dialling the display down means shrinking in a way that reads as sulking, and explaining it in advance sounds like somebody describing their own charisma. so the gap keeps being discovered in person, one guest at a time.
cost: unconditional room, immediately, to people who have not earned it and are not going to be assessed — that is the rarest thing on the list and the last thing anyone asks for. they wanted the other thing. so the gratitude runs a beat behind, years behind sometimes, and arrives from people who have long since stopped coming.

lead: you have ended two lives completely and nobody attended either. an opening has no door to shut, so the most total changes you have made registered outside as nothing — the same welcome, the same week, a person quietly replaced.
sun: an ending needs a boundary to happen at, and you do not keep one. so the whole of it occurs inside: the position abandoned, the belief dropped, the person you were finished with — all of it done thoroughly, in one ordinary week, with the room open the entire time and the same people walking through it. nothing on the outside carries a mark. an announcement would require closing something first.
moon: what changed did not change partially. the previous version is gone at the root — its taste, its allegiances, its reasons — and every arrangement that version entered is intact, because the room never closed and the people in it were never told. so they go on addressing somebody who is not present, and being answered warmly by the stranger who inherited the address.
pull: the person they are fond of has been gone for years and answers all their messages. you cannot report a death when the body kept every appointment.
tension: people call you steady, and the word fits nobody worse. from outside you have not changed since your twenties — same door, same warmth, same availability — while inside, three complete replacements have gone through without a witness. the ones who love the earliest version are loyal to a photograph. correcting them would take closing the room long enough for the difference to show, and closing is the one motion you have never had.
cost: you can end a thing without taking anyone down with it — no scene, no sides, no year of people asking what happened, the entire demolition absorbed on your side and the room open throughout. no part of it transfers. the person who did those years with you cannot be told they are being remembered by somebody who was not there for any of it.

lead: half the work in your life is finished, in use, and signed by other people. you supplied the push and the room it needed, and neither of those shows up in a finished object.
sun: the making needs somewhere to happen, and the somewhere is your half of it. you clear a place, the thing gets built standing in it, and afterwards the place is invisible under the thing — nobody looks at a built thing and asks what room it was assembled in. so the part you supplied is the only part with no surface, and it is load-bearing in every direction.
moon: The Hand deals in impulse, and an impulse takes the shape of whoever received it. within a month it is theirs — they can feel it running, they can describe how they came to it, and the description is honest. the push does not stay attached to the person who gave it. it becomes their momentum, and momentum has no provenance in it at all.
pull: everything you have made is out there working, under other names. a push and a room are the two contributions that leave no mark on the thing they produced.
tension: the account is that you have not done much of your own, and it is delivered kindly, usually by someone listing what you helped with. the list is the evidence against them and reads as evidence for them. proving otherwise would mean producing the version where you were not there, and that version does not exist anywhere it could be examined — the projects all happened, whole, on schedule, with your part folded invisibly into their foundations.
cost: people arrive stuck and leave in motion, and the transfer is clean enough that nobody feels handled. none of it can be traced back afterwards. you finish with a working knowledge of how nearly everything around you got built, and nothing on a shelf you can point at and say where that one began.

lead: the person who loved you most spent a year trying to get in, and there was no getting in to do. what they wanted was the inside, and the inside has been in plain view since the beginning.
sun: an opening has one width, the same width for everybody. there is no second, narrower way through that you could offer somebody as a mark of trust, because nothing was ever routed around the first one. so the usual way of getting close — being let past a thing other people are not let past — has nothing to work with here. everyone is at one distance from you.
moon: the bright thing is on the outside of you and needs no permission to look at, so they arrive already having had the best of it. wanting more is the next move and there is no more — no reserved portion, no version kept back for the ones who stay. they read it as being held at arm's length, the only explanation on offer, and it fits nothing you did.
pull: the ones who love you have exactly what a stranger has, and no closer place exists to promise them. everything worth having was visible from outside on the first day.
tension: someone who met you at a party and someone who has known you for twenty years will describe you in nearly the same words, and both descriptions are accurate. easy to know, people say, meaning it kindly, and it lands as a ceiling on the long one — who cannot show what those years bought. they bought company, which is real, and no further access, because none was ever held back to be granted later.
cost: anyone can size you up in ten minutes and be right, and nobody who stays ten years finds anything different underneath. the gesture that makes a person feel chosen — the thing said to one and not the rest — has no material to be made from, so what you offer instead is the same brightness, at the same distance, for as long as they want it.

lead: there is a place everyone you know belongs to, and the ground under it is yours. membership was never issued to the person holding the room, and thirty years in, nobody has thought to ask.
sun: the place where they all met each other is one you cleared. they date friendships to it, they know exactly what night they walked in. a place is not a party to what happens inside it, so the thing everyone else took from the arrangement — a group they are in — is the one thing it cannot give back to whoever made the room.
moon: not needing the room is not a stance you took, and nothing about it shows. you are present every time, which is what devotion looks like from outside, so nobody has had cause to check. and there is nothing to find: you have never resented an evening of it and have never wanted out. the attachment never formed, in the one person the whole thing is organised around.
pull: you built the place everyone belongs to and you have never belonged to it. nobody has noticed, because you have not missed a single night.
tension: a decade of nights and no absences gets read as loyalty, and the conclusion is generous and wrong in a way that cannot be corrected out loud. the honest version would take something from people who did get the thing, and the thing they got is not fake. so it goes unsaid, and every year you are described more warmly as the heart of a room you could leave tomorrow and not feel gone from.
cost: your place has no politics in it, because the one person who could set the terms wants nothing from the group. what you built cannot be built for you. an invitation is worthless to someone who was never outside, so the years go by with everyone fed at your table, and the one thing you supply is the one thing nobody can hand to you.

lead: you got there in the end, and the end was eleven years late. The Claws never put either load down, and the room you keep never got tight enough to make that necessary.
sun: most people choose because they run out of somewhere to put the second thing. you do not run out. the room takes both of them whole, indefinitely, and taking them is not experienced as effort, so the moment where one of the two has to go never arrives. what other people call deciding is mostly scarcity doing the work for them, and that machinery is not fitted to you.
moon: each load gets the whole of you in alternation, so both come out finished and both come out after the moment that wanted them. the second thing never stops the first. it stands in front of it for a year, then swaps, and by the time either one is ready to be shown, the people who asked have solved it some other way.
pull: you have two finished lives and both of them are late. nothing ever ran out in time to make you pick, so you arrived complete, years after the room had moved on.
tension: people who watched you keep a second thing alive for a decade without ever pushing it land on hedging, and from where they stand it fits. what they are looking at is two full commitments in a life sized for one, and the only visible symptom is that everything takes twice as long. slowness looks like doubt from any distance. the finished work would answer it, and the finished work is, by construction, not ready yet.
cost: two things at full weight, neither of them a hobby, neither degraded by the other's existence, and you have held both for thirty years. the market for any of it has a date on it. by the time both halves are ready to be seen together, the thing that would have used them was assembled years ago by someone with one idea and no patience.

lead: nobody agreed to anything. they took the room you had open on an ordinary evening, left having had a good night of it, and it has been binding on your side ever since.
sun: an opening asks nothing at the entrance, so nothing gets settled there. no terms, no length, no statement of what the thing is for — it begins at whatever width it found and runs at that width. the conversation that would have turned it into an agreement is the one your side has never needed from anybody, and nothing later supplies it.
moon: The Crown keeps whatever it is given, and it was given this. what walked in gets held to the decade — dates carried, absences absorbed, the apparatus of a promise running behind something nobody proposed. on their side there is no undertaking to breach, so they are free the whole length of it, doing nothing wrong, inside a commitment that exists in one person.
pull: you have kept every promise you were never asked to make. the other party cannot break one, cannot renew one, and has no idea there is anything to be inside of.
tension: one of them treats it lightly. nothing exists to point at — no date, no undertaking, no sentence said out loud — so raising it now means writing terms after the fact, which comes out sounding like a person inventing an obligation for somebody else to carry. the keeping runs at the weight it always ran at, and which of the two of you is further in stays a private matter, held by the one who is.
cost: hand you something with no record on it — a key, a number, a promise about somebody's child — and it runs in you exactly as a filed one would. the mechanism never checks whether anyone asked. so you are held by arrangements that were never proposed, and no release comes, since a release has to come from a party who knows they were holding you.

lead: the hardest thing anyone could say to you would be received, and everybody knows it, and in twenty years the sentence has not made it across the table — it gets stopped somewhere else, by people who are not you.
sun: the offer is real. no subject is out of order with you, nothing has to be brought carefully, a person can come straight at the thing with no preparation, and you have meant that since you were young. what the room cannot do is remove what was here before it. the openness sits on top of a position, and the position is not addressed by anything the openness does.
moon: the eldest is useful to everybody who is not it, so the room defends the position without being asked to. whoever comes at you gets cooled by their own people, in a car on the way home, talked round and told they were tired and quietly dropped a place down the list of who gets rung. what reaches you is that they have drifted.
pull: the openness has never been tested, and the reason is not you. somebody tried, once, and was handled by the others before it got anywhere near your table.
tension: what circulates about you is that you can be told anything, and it circulates among people who watched somebody test it and saw what came after. there was a price and you did not charge it, so no part of that lesson is yours to overturn. a position defended offstage cannot be resigned onstage either: saying out loud that you want no rank in the room is exactly the kind of sentence only the ranking person gets to say.
cost: the failure reaches you while it is small and unpresentable, before anyone has decided what to call it, because coming to you takes no preparation and no standing. that access is bought with an offer you cannot honour. the one report that would tell you whether any of it is sound — somebody coming at you directly — has been intercepted for two decades before arrival.

lead: The Root goes down until it meets something that will not move, and then it has its answer. in you it goes down and meets more room, and the digging has been running since you were young.
sun: other excavations end at a fixed thing — a parent, an injury, one settled fact about a person that will not shift — and the fixed thing becomes both the explanation and the place the shovel stops. nothing in you performs that function. there is room under every layer, so the search goes past the depth where a person is supposed to arrive at their own bedrock and carries on into more of the same.
moon: the digging carries no rule of its own for stopping, so what comes up is a run of true findings, each accurate, none final. the cause under the cause turns out to have a cause. every answer you have brought up about yourself is correct and none of it presses on anything, because whatever you find has space around it, and space does not hold a finding in place.
pull: there is no rock at the bottom of you. you have the true reason for what you do, three versions of it, each one accurate, and the doing has not changed.
tension: everyone who loves you has a theory that would finish the matter, and you can take all of them in, agree with the good ones, and come out operating the way you operated before. from where they sit that reads as sliding out of it. someone who resists an explanation can be argued with; someone who accepts one and is unaltered gives the other side nothing to push against, and it ends with them deciding you were humouring them.
cost: somebody can finish a sentence with you that they have never finished anywhere, in one sitting, and hear the actual cause said back in the same hour without anything narrowing. turned inward the same equipment produces an account of you rewritten every few years, each version true, none of them the last, and nothing underneath to consult when you have to know what you would do.

lead: the one everybody warns you about arrives at yours and there is no incident, ever. the same absence works on pairs, and by the time you hear about that part, one of the two has stopped coming.
sun: they arrive braced for a demand that never comes. the behaviour everybody else has a strategy for answers something — a schedule to fit, a size to come down to, somebody managing the evening — and none of it is present, so the behaviour does not come out. that is not you handling them well. there is nothing for it to answer, which is why your account of them gets waved off.
moon: The Flock separates, and here the separating is done by arithmetic rather than by anyone's decision. a pair holds partly because there is nowhere else to put the heavy thing, and your place is somewhere else. the half that arrives loaded sets it down with you, it lands fine, and the other one's whole position — the only person who could take that — quietly stops being true.
pull: nothing at your place breaks a pair. it removes the reason one of them was necessary, which is slower, and which the two of them will spend a year arguing about without mentioning you.
tension: the credit comes from one side — you were good for her, said warmly, meant — and the other one goes, and neither account has an event in it, because there was not one. you can see the next one from the first evening: which half arrives lighter each time, how long the other has been the whole supply. heading it off would mean being less available to one of two people who have done nothing wrong.
cost: the person other people schedule around comes to you and is ordinary, for years, with no method involved and nothing to keep up, which cannot be taught to anybody who asks how you do it. it works on the arrangement they came in as well. what you host is a slow dissolving that nobody attends, and you get told afterwards by whichever half kept your number.

lead: both of them called you that week, and both talked for an hour, and letting each one finish took no effort of any kind — nothing in you was pulling for an outcome.
sun: a place with no side in it is rare enough that people will drive an hour to sit in one. so the argument comes to your room. they arrive with it already loaded and set it down where it does not have to be won first, and both of them do that, and each assumes the room was theirs for the evening.
moon: and both accounts are kept. what a blank does with two versions of one night is hold them at the size each was told, without either wearing the other down, for lack of anything already in place to check them against. so you carry his account of the marriage and hers, whole, for years, and the contradiction never resolves into a view.
pull: you can hold the wedding and the divorce in the same room, at the same table, and be honest at both, because nothing in you was ever on anybody's side.
tension: fair is the word, and it is meant kindly, and it is why neither of them ever stopped coming. fairness was never the thing anybody needed. a person in the middle of the worst year they have had wants someone who has gone stupid on their behalf, and that requires a prior refusal to hear the other one. you heard the other one. you always do, and it takes nothing out of you, and they can feel that.
cost: people in the middle of something come to you first and stay longest, because your place asks nobody to arrive with a position already settled. the same evening is available to the other party. thirty years of this and the people closest to you have never had you on their side — you were where they went, and where the other one went too.

lead: by the time anyone tells you, the room has been ready for a season. what The Listener picks up cannot be acted on out loud, so it goes into the one thing you can adjust without explaining: width.
sun: space is the one move you can make without giving a reason. a cleared evening explains itself as an ordinary quiet week; an offer to take the kids reads as an offer. so you act on what you picked up by moving the one thing nobody checks, and the move is in place long before there is an event to attach it to. from outside, the timing is luck.
moon: the hearing takes no permission. you get the shape of somebody's next year off a pause in a sentence about a car, and there is no procedure for that — it cannot be brought to them and cannot be unheard, so it converts into furniture: a standing invitation, a key left behind, a night kept free every week for a reason you never give.
pull: they came out the other side of it thinking that year happened to be a gentle one. you heard it coming in the autumn. nobody has ever been told they were seen.
tension: the phrase is that you always seem to have time, and it gets said with a small amount of envy in it, as though your life came pre-cleared. it did not. every open week in it was opened deliberately, on information you got by accident, for a person who had not yet worked out they were in trouble. explaining that would require repeating the sentence you heard it in, back to the one who said it, months later.
cost: nobody has to ask you for anything, and nobody has to be in a state worth asking from — the help is standing there when they turn around, sized right, already paid for. what they miss is the part that would have consoled them most. a person carried through a bad year by an arrangement they never noticed comes out of it believing they were alone in it and managed.

lead: eleven years of the same night every week, and it has no name, no list, no one in charge of it. what holds it up is that you keep showing up and setting the pace.
sun: nothing about it can hold anybody. no one signed anything, no one could resign, and that is the reason they come — an evening with no claim on you gets attended by people who would turn down an invitation. so the whole structure sits on recurrence. there is no place, only a night that keeps happening, and the happening has one source.
moon: a beat is the only fastener the thing has, and a beat has to be produced every week or it does not exist. people synchronise to it without consenting to anything — they know what they are doing on that night for a year out — and because there is nothing to belong to, nobody experiences it as depending on you. they experience it as a night that exists.
pull: there is nothing holding it up but the fact that you turn up. finding out would take stopping, and stopping is the same experiment as ending it.
tension: the thing everybody says about it is that it runs itself, and they are not flattering you — they genuinely cannot see a mechanism, because the mechanism is a person arriving. one month away, and nothing collapses in any way anyone could date. attendance thins, the night moves, and by winter there was never anything there to have ended. no obituary, no fallout, no argument about whose fault it was.
cost: a decade of people staying in each other's lives, with nobody having to organise, remember, or commit to anything — the pulse does all of it. no part of it accrues to you. eleven years of holding a scene together produces no scene that is yours, and the day the count drops, what disappears gets filed by everybody as time passing.

lead: most people have one furnished thing in them — a temper, an appetite, a talent that takes up space. The Void arrives here with no counterweight, and there is nothing in you for a room to catch on.
sun: nobody checks what kind of week you are having. there has never been a kind — no weather to read on the way over, nothing to be timed around. so they arrive at any hour with the whole of their own week and the evening takes the shape of what they brought, every time, and the account they give of it afterwards has everybody in it except the person whose kitchen it was.
moon: from inside there is no weather either. nothing presses, nothing objects, nothing has ever been in the way of anything else — you have never had to get past yourself to do a thing, and you have never been started by anything either. the day is available the moment it opens, every day, at the same width, which is why one is hard to tell from the next.
pull: nothing in you has ever been in the way. nothing in you has ever been the reason either. it goes all the way down, undiluted, and there has never been anything else to be.
tension: at some point people stop asking how you are, because the answer has been the same for as long as they have known you, and they take that for peace. peace implies something that was quieted. nothing here was ever loud enough to need quieting, and correcting it would take producing the thing that got mastered, so the admiration holds, gets warmer with the years, and what they are praising is the shape of a room.
cost: you can sit with somebody in the worst hour of their life and want nothing from them, which almost nobody manages past twenty minutes. it runs the other way too. nobody has ever had to move a week around your state, or ask what you needed, or find out they had got it wrong — and that is most of what people mean when they say they know someone.

lead: the one who came to yours to disappear was safe the whole time they were there, and so was the person they were disappearing from, who had the same welcome on a different night.
sun: a hiding place works by leaving somebody outside it. you have room, so you have somewhere for a person to be while their life is unlivable — the spare year, the address nobody has — and the thing that would make it a hiding place, a name you decline to give and a face you turn away, is the one part of the equipment you were not issued.
moon: The Hideaway hands over the instinct whole: you know within an hour who needs putting somewhere, and you put them there, and the arrangement holds up on you alone. what it withholds is the other half — the sentence that keeps a person out. the evening that hides one of them is available to whoever they left, at the same warmth, and neither of them is being betrayed.
pull: you can keep anybody. you cannot keep anybody out, and it is one gesture doing both, so the safest place your friends have is also the address their trouble walks into.
tension: open house, people say, warmly, and the ones saying it have never had anything worth concealing. the ones who did learned the shape of it early — a good month at yours, then a quieter arrangement with somebody who owns a lock. nothing ever leaked; you would take a secret to the grave and everybody knows that. what you cannot be is hard to find, and being hard to find is most of what a hiding place is.
cost: somebody can arrive at yours with a suitcase and no explanation prepared, stay however long it runs, and never be asked what they did. protection here is one person deep. it holds exactly as long as nobody tests it, and the day the other one comes up your path you will let them in, because letting people in is the whole of what you have.

lead: one wall is not a room, and one wall is what gets built here, permanently, out of proper materials — so people move in behind the thing you solved for them and treat the rest of the horizon as covered.
sun: what you put up is real and it is single. the material goes into exactly the thing that was wrong when they arrived — the debt, the visa, the place to live — and it holds for decades, because building it took nothing out of you and enclosing anybody further never occurred to you as work. the other three directions are as open as your ground was before they came.
moon: nothing The Chamber puts up is experienced as partial. people behind one of your walls relax the way anybody relaxes indoors — they stop watching the direction it covers, and they stop watching the other three as well, because being housed does not itemise. the second trouble finds them undefended, in your care, having been genuinely saved from the first.
pull: one thing solved permanently, and no perimeter around it. they were rescued from what was coming and left standing in the open for what came instead.
tension: the complaint comes from the person who owes you the most, which is why it takes years to arrive. you settled something enormous for them and did not ring for eighteen months afterwards. from inside your arrangement the enormous thing is the arrangement — it is up, it is holding, nothing about it needs attending. what they wanted next was small and repeated, and small repeated things are the one kind of structure you have never put up.
cost: a stranger's catastrophe gets a permanent answer from you within a season, funded and built, with no relationship required first. everyone you know turned up in a year that had to be salvaged. nobody comes to yours in an ordinary week, because ordinary weeks have nothing in them that needs putting up, and the one direction you have covered is the only one anybody has ever stood in with you.

lead: nobody keeps the middle of the journey. they keep where they left and where they ended up, and the year in between — the one that happened at your place — comes out of the account as a gap.
sun: a crossing needs somewhere to be in the middle of it, and that is the whole of your contribution and the reason it works. a person between two lives has no occupation, no address and no account of themselves, and every other door requires at least one of those. yours requires nothing, so they arrive with nothing and are short of nothing while they are there.
moon: The Guide finishes the delivery — the job in the other city, the second marriage, the thing they had been failing at for a decade — and the route to it ran through your place for fourteen months. arrival retires the middle. the more completely somebody lands, the more completely that year becomes the stretch they were getting through.
pull: you are the part of the story that gets summarised. everyone you have carried remembers the leaving and the arriving, and a warmth in the middle with no address on it.
tension: you enable it gets said, usually by a sister or a partner, and there is a version of the ledger where that is exactly right. nothing at yours makes the next stretch urgent — no rent that hurts, no date, no question at breakfast about the plan. some of them cross in a season and some take four years, and the difference is not something you have ever been able to see from inside it.
cost: a person with no job, no story and nothing to be introduced as can sit at your table for a year while nobody asks what the plan is. the crossing is what gets kept. you hold the part of people's lives they are relieved to have finished, so the affection that comes to you is real and dated to a period they do not visit.

lead: for eleven years his mother has known how he is, in his own words, through you — and the two of them have not spoken. The Thread runs to whatever length is required and takes nothing off what it carries.
sun: everything that crosses a person picks up whatever that person is carrying — a grudge, a preference for one of the two, a version they would rather be true. yours goes across unmodified, at the temperature it was handed over in, because there is nothing in the way of it. so both ends get accurate weather about the other one for decades, and neither has to soften anything on the way.
moon: a line carries the load and keeps none of it. the news of the death, the apology neither could word, the money — all of it goes through you undiminished and lands on somebody else. you were present for the sending and for the arrival, which nobody else was. nothing goes the other way. there has never been a message with your own business in it.
pull: the heaviest sentences three families ever produced went through you word for word. no part of that traffic was ever addressed to the line it was travelling on.
tension: one of them works it out eventually and puts it to you as an accusation: that a decade of accurate reporting is why neither ever had to make the call. it holds up. a conversation that can be had through somebody does not get had, and the ease of the route is the entire reason. no answer exists that does not sound like a person defending their position, and the position pays nothing.
cost: two people who have not spoken since the funeral can stay exactly current with each other through you, at no cost to either, for the rest of their lives. none of it accrues. what you have with each of them is made out of the other one, so both would describe you as close family, and neither could give an account of your year.
